title: Echo
note: a pulse sounds on its own and its echoes return off the walls, again and again. tap to open the walls and let them out. the pulses keep coming. after Haruki Murakami

title: Optional
note: strikes land on their own and pass on their own; hold one and it darkens, bleeds, spreads. let go and it fades. after Haruki Murakami

title: Free to Choose
note: forms drift freely; each one reaching the line chooses, cross and be marked, or turn away. need grows the longer it waits. after Santiago Sierra, Salamanca, 2000

title: One Line
note: one framed canvas; one continuous white line draws big rounded loops on blush ground; tap to redraw

title: Weather
note: rain, wind and fog over scorched paper; tap to change the weather

title: Constellations
note: a night sky; trace the flame across the stars to draw the figures

title: Sleeping village
note: a hamlet asleep under the moon; set a roof alight and watch it burn out

title: Candles and lanterns
note: a dark room of candles; light them one by one and lanterns rise

title: Garden
note: grass and flowers sway; walk through to flatten them, burn a patch to ash

title: Ink and embroidery
note: words in flowing ink; splash blots, dry them to cracks with fire

title: Spider web
note: a tensioned web; every touch plucks the threads and dew drops flash

title: Bioluminescent water
note: a real wave simulation; rings spread and interfere where you touch

title: Mycelium
note: hyphae wander, branch and glow from every touch, then fade

title: Firefly hunt
note: glowing motes drift and dodge your finger; catch one and it flares

title: Magma crust
note: dark rock, glowing veins; touch heats it through red to white

title: Grid
note: a faint drafting grid, ninety pixels to the square

title: Frozen lake
note: steps crack the ice; cracks branch, glow, then heal

title: Long exposure
note: drag to paint light; the plate holds it and slowly fades

title: Topographic map
note: contour lines of living terrain, hills rising under your finger

title: Circuit board
note: pulses race down copper traces, lit by touch

title: Freestyle Basketball
note: a chibi juggler freestyles a basketball through painted streets, in rhythm, every frame brushed live

title: The River
note: a river of golden light flows between two radiant blooms on opposite banks - they face each other across it, never crossing

title: Rooted
note: a field of golden blooms leans toward a pale moon it can never reach - petals drift up and dissolve before arriving

title: Ribbons
note: six ribbons of colour drift, undulate, and pass through each other - pure form and colour, no story

title: The Other Side
note: the travellers who crossed the membrane weave light into the other side - every crossing leaves light behind

title: Through
note: gold travellers cross a luminous membrane and emerge blue on the other side - sometimes the only way to the other end is through it

title: The Still Point
note: a field in turmoil holds still at its center - the question does not argue with the noise, after Gadamer

title: The Circle
note: concentric rings turn at their own speeds, each reading returns changed - the hermeneutic circle, after Gadamer

title: The Bend
note: a precise grid bent by invisible currents - what was said never arrives straight, after Gadamer

title: Through Your Own Past
note: words fall through veils of memory, each layer tinting and fragmenting them - after Gadamer

title: Where Horizons Meet
note: two horizons drift and overlap - meaning ignites only where they meet, after Gadamer

title: The Fusion of Horizons
note: spoken marks cross a field of interpretation and arrive reassembled - after Gadamer

title: The Rolling Stone
note: infinite zoom stone loop

title: Rumor of a Turn
note: Twelve pale-gold koi; tap to startle one and the turn ripples through the school. After Job Talle's turn-contagion.

title: Squares
note: Hans's 5x5 coin-flip sketch, placed as-is.

title: Petal Weather
note: A night meadow where flowers open in slow traveling waves of amber, poppy and ivory; drag to stir the field, tap for a new meadow.

title: Tumblewood
note: Fifty-six leaves tumble down a lamplit forest corridor, each falling at its own pace; drag to stir the wind, tap for a new fall.

title: Downtown First
note: A city block wakes up after dark, starting downtown and rippling outward, and you can stir the windows with a drag.

title: The Long Drift
note: A slow drift through a diagonal lane of cosmic dust, with near grains sliding past far stars at eight times the speed.

title: Nightwatch
note: A lighthouse beam keeps strict time over a dark sea, and the water only remembers the light for a few seconds.

title: Swell Line
note: A slow swell bends the horizon line, and the setting sun and reed silhouettes melt into the sea and pull back out again.

title: Curtain Drift
note: Curtains of light breathe over black water, mirrored beneath the horizon; drag to gust the field, tap for fresh curtains.

title: The Sinking Hour
note: A desert dusk driven by one number: the sun's altitude sets shadow length, wind speed, and sky color as it sinks from 38 degrees to below the horizon over three minutes.

title: Summit First
note: First light crosses a dark eastern ridge, finds the summit, and washes down the face while the lake holds it all a second time.

title: Entrainment
note: Four hundred fireflies on individual clocks nudge their phase toward every flash they see, so the field breathes from chaos into traveling waves of synchrony. Drag to tear desync through the waves and watch them heal. Tap to scatter all phases and watch order return.

title: The Same River
note: After Hans's Heraclitus quote (No man ever steps in the same river twice): a meandering river channel whose course migrates over time, advecting silt particles on fading trails; the current never repeats. Watch first, drag to step in and bend the current into eddies, tap to turn the river over.

title: Metaballs
note: Animated metaballs on paper: wandering field sources merge and split as thick black outlines, watch first, drag to add a field source, tap to reseed.

title: Marble Atlas
note: A procedurally assembled chain reaction across four worlds. Row, climb, swing and roll between connected machines: docking bridges, pressure keys, tipping decks and earned gate releases. Original reactive piano; no final frame.

title: The Last Light
note: A glass ember wakes a forgotten foundry, flowers in a sunlit glasshouse, and constellations beneath a moonlit observatory. One marble, three living chapters, 21 real kinetic acts, endlessly reimagined.

title: Smoke From Nowhere
note: After the Modern Rogue smoke trick: a match strikes low, the flame dies, and the smoke it leaves behind is the piece — curling plumes that bloom, drift, and dissolve, never the same shape twice. Drag to stir the smoke.

title: Five Up, Turn
note: After Salvo Stassi: five balls on a juggler who travels the space, turns full 360s under high throws, kicks balls blind off the foot, and crosses into mills mess.

title: Two Tables, One Marble
note: One red glass marble crosses two tables in a single take: track curves, a rainbow domino line, a blue spinner gate, a seesaw, a gap, and a drop into a star-marked box.

title: Binary
note: A clock told in flipping discs: brass for a lit bit, a ghost ring for a dark one. When the seconds roll over, the flip ripples left through minutes and hours. Tap to hide the digits.

title: The Juggler
note: After Luther Bangert: a juggler in black on a warm stage, five white balls in a true cascade. The hands do the real work — catch wide, scoop low, throw from inside. Watch only.

title: Inkwell
note: Ink dropped in dark water: slow blooms open, curl, and dissolve on a seamless loop. Watch only.

title: Linkwork III
note: Third study after the forged wall sculpture, rebuilt from the chain: crisp rectangular links flowing horizontally, each passing alternately over and under its neighbours. A slow ripple travels the chain; double-tap re-forges it.

title: Linkwork II
note: Second study after the forged wall sculpture: a denser, more tangled cluster of bronze and blackened-steel links. A slow light sweep crosses the metal; double-tap re-forges it.

title: Linkwork
note: After the forged wall sculpture: interlocking bronze and blackened-steel links, hand-hammered, each at its own depth. A slow light sweep crosses the metal; double-tap re-forges it.

title: Pinwheel Quilt II
note: Closer to the hand-drawn original: portrait lattice, stronger swirl, wilder warp. A seamless loop; double-tap re-sews it.

title: Pinwheel Quilt
note: Ink pinwheels on a warped lattice, after a hand-drawn quilt. A seamless loop; double-tap re-sews it.

title: Perigee
note: One closed harmonograph orbit, one traveler. A seamless loop.

title: Gossamer
note: Verlet silk on a slow wind field. Drag to disturb it.

title: Cipher
note: Code-drawn glyphs orbit in concentric rings at different speeds. Drag to stir; double-tap to reseed.

title: Ember Knot
note: Luminous particles stream along a torus knot on near-black, colored like cooling embers. Drag to orbit; double-tap to reset.

title: Ripples
note: Overlapping wave fields drawn as a breathing field of ink dots on paper. Drag to drop a stone; double-tap for new waves.

title: Rhizome
note: A root network that grows, prunes itself, and is reborn in breathing seasons. Drag to bend the growth; double-tap to reseed.

title: Split Tide
note: A recursive subdivision that breathes on a seamless loop. Drag to scrub time.

title: Confluence
note: Two ink currents cross an evolving flow field. Drag to stir, double-tap to reseed.

title: Shear
note: Diagonal bars and wedges on a leaning energy band. Tap to flip.

title: Fission
note: Recursive subdivision grid, splitting and healing. Tap to divide.

title: Murmur
note: Luminous particles coalesce into a glowing ring, hold, and dissolve. A seamless loop.

title: Curl
note: Luminous particles ride a curl-noise current on near-black, drawing the undertow itself.

title: Afterglow
note: Blazing sunset sky over dark silhouette land, thick palette-knife bands, after Jason Anderson.

title: Swell
note: Thick impasto seascape: foam-white horizon over deep teal water, after Jason Anderson.

title: Concrete
note: Hard-edge geometric shapes on a strict grid, slowly reconfiguring. Tap to rearrange.

title: Impasto
note: Thick palette-knife color blocks in a stained-glass jigsaw, after Jason Anderson.

title: Broken Rings
note: Dashed rings interfere until the field seems to move; one ring burns vermilion. Click for another shimmer.

title: Compass
note: Needles lean with a seeded weather of direction; the vertical ones turn rust. Click for another compass.

title: Truchet
note: Coin-flip tiles chain their arcs into paths nobody drew. Click for another quarter turn.

title: Warp
note: A checkerboard bulging under two crossing waves. Click for another warp.

title: Hatch
note: One family of lines, swelling and thinning around a hidden light. Click for another hatch.

title: Raster
note: A strict dot grid sized by two rings arguing. Click for another raster.

title: Well
note: Squares turn a little further as they shrink, down a twisting shaft. Click for another well.

title: Solstice
note: A low vermilion sun, warm rays up and cool rays down. Click for another solstice.

title: Orchard
note: Packed canopies from above, big trees first, fruit in rust. Click for another orchard.

title: Alluvium
note: River mouths spill fans of sediment that overlap and settle over each other. Click for another alluvium.

title: Strays
note: Meridians bend around slow vortices; the strays burn warmer. Click for another meridian.

title: Silt
note: Layers of earth settle, darken with depth, and slip once along a pale seam. Click for another silt.

title: Undertow
note: Rings bent by a slow current crowd into dark bands. Click for another undertow.

title: Faultline
note: The curves are banned: hard turns, bold faults, sudden slips. Click for another fault.

title: Grainfield
note: Twenty-five thousand dots settle where the current bends. Click for another field.

title: Tension
note: Threads strung on nested rings, pulled taut or left slack; gold warps over the weave. Click for another weaving.

title: Driftlines
note: Hairline currents; tone drawn from the water's speed. Click for another drift.

title: Underdrawing
note: The scaffolding first, then the paint. Watch it build, click to rebuild.

title: Hundred
note: A fixed edition of one hundred prints. Click to walk the edition.

title: Crosscurrent
note: Dark and pale ribbons ride the same current and never touch. Click for a new current.

title: Patch Mountain
note: A mountain built from nothing but patches: directional color strokes on a reserved dark ground, no outlines anywhere.

title: Folded Light
note: One palette, three panels, three moods.

title: Marine Snow
note: The dropped 9055s background polished into its own piece: a quiet water column with slanting light shafts, layered drifting marine snow, and a whisper of distant glow. No creature.

title: Meridian
note: Flowing meridian lines in blue-violet. Drag to stir.

title: Dusk Shore
note: A pixel-art beach from above at dusk, drawn with code. The shoreline breathes, wave bands drift, sun glitter twinkles gold, and tiny figures wait at the foam edge.

title: Misregister
note: One geometric form pulled three times in cyan, magenta and yellow, each plate offset like a misregistered print. The color is the misregistration.

title: Plain Weave
note: Warp and weft threads crossing in plain weave. Each thread alternates over and under at every crossing, like real cloth.

title: Ruled Lines
note: Dense hand-drawn rules in ballpoint blue on paper. A hidden field lifts the lines — the ghost of a circular presence you feel before you see.

title: Tidepool Contours
note: A rock shelf at low tide, read as depth bands. The pools breathe, small crabs work the wet rock, and a click drops a pebble.

title: The Shadow of One Letter
note: A red wireframe solid, hand-drawn, casting a shadow built from one repeated dot. The shadow's edge and density do the drawing. Click for another casting.

title: Eternal Bloom
note: Continuous spawn every 2s: squares expand and rotate at uniform rates, alternating direction.

title: Deliberately Uninteresting
note: After Sol LeWitt. Thousands of identical marks; the composition lives in coverage, never in the mark. Up close it is nothing but handwriting, at distance a curve. Click for another field.

title: Square Fountain
note: Hypnotic loop: squares spawn center, grow and rotate, dissolve at max size.

title: What Is Generative Art
note: The artist writes the rules, the machine rolls the dice, and a family comes out. One branching system, six children, one keeper. Click for another family.

title: Smoke
note: One breath, made visible. A single column of smoke rises, widens, and dissolves into empty paper. Click for another.

title: River Stones
note: A quiet bed of river stones, each water-worn smooth, overlaps deepening honestly. One moss-green stone among the gray. Click for another arrangement.

title: Frost
note: First frost on the pane. Ink-blue crystals creep in from the corners and stop, leaving the middle clear to breathe. Click for another morning.

title: Lunar Strip
note: One lunation in twenty-nine moons, waxing to a gold full moon and waning again, each terminator hand-wobbled. Click for another sky.

title: Crows on a Wire
note: Five on the wire and one just leaving. A small moment, drawn plainly, under a big empty sky. Click for another morning.

title: Wind Field
note: A gust frozen mid-passage through wheat, every blade leaning downwind, the bend swelling where the gust is strongest. One red poppy stands unbent. Click for another field.

title: Slat Light
note: Low sun through a fence, the sun itself offstage. Long soft shadows rake across paper, deepening where they overlap, and one warm band falls where a slat is missing. Click for another evening.

title: Square One
note: One square: its sides unwrap into a single line as it turns, then fold back.

title: Unison
note: Continuous spawn every 2s: all squares rotate the same direction.

title: Sides
note: Dot becomes line, triangle, square, gains sides until a circle, returns to dot.

title: Sides II
note: Dot to circle, skipping sides: readable polygons then a quick rush to round.

title: Halved
note: One random polygon. Draw a line through it and every polygon the line crosses splits in two, in tonal steps. Cut as far as you like.

title: Trellis
note: Type any word and watch it grow into a hedge, leaves and blossoms along every letter, the word still readable through the green.

title: Flight Deck
note: Seven fogged depth levels of swirling particle trails, flown through like gates. Click to jump to a fresh system; move the pointer to look around.

title: Personal Weather
note: A field of wind barbs, each with a heading of its own. Your pointer paints weather into the air: fast flicks burn amber, slow drifts stay blue. Move your pointer to stir it.

title: Accumulation
note: Sixteen thousand grains of light dropped one by one until a moon, a ridge, a wave, or a forest gathers out of the dust. Click the piece for a new sky.

title: Subdivide
note: A rectangle keeps splitting until every piece earns a texture: hatching, stipple, rings, the odd flat solid. Only adjacent to Mondrian in method. Click the piece for a new variation.

title: Contour Fields
note: Contour lines over imaginary terrain, each drawn a little unsteadily so they read as hand inked. They bunch up where the ground gets steep. Click the piece for a new variation.

title: Mai Menochot
note: A rising sun in two passes of ink over still water, the rust pass deliberately misregistered like a slipped letterpress bed. Click the piece for a new variation.

title: Three Shapes
note: A tangent chain of circles, squares, and triangles in two inks, construction lines left visible. Click the piece for a new variation.

title: Strata Break
note: Concentric rings dissolving from order into chaos, with one red ring. Click the piece for a new variation.

title: Moiré
note: Wheels of fine lines turn at different speeds, and where they cross, new patterns bloom and dissolve. This one moves. Click the piece for a new variation.

title: Oscillons
note: Waveforms drawn the way an oscilloscope draws them, layered in phosphor tones on dark. Click the piece for a new variation.

title: Bloom
note: Exact geometry in ink first, then watercolor washes bloom over it and dry where they want. Click the piece for a fresh sheet.

title: Growth
note: A line that follows only local rules grows into folds no hand would draw. This one grows while you watch. Click the piece for a new growth.

title: Murmuration
note: Six hundred particles hold a word that shivers but never lands, until a gust scatters them and they find their letters again. This one moves. Click the piece for a new word.

title: Congregation
note: A living web of three hundred forty seeds that breathes with its own synthesized heartbeat, gathering at every kick. This one moves and makes sound. Click the piece to start it.

title: Tone Mosaic
note: An etching pressed from a thousand voronoi cells, where cell size does all the shading. Click the piece for a new plate.

title: Corridor
note: A quadtree of geometric motifs, camera-projected into an endless corridor. This one moves. Click the piece for a new corridor.

title: Field Notes
note: Wind, recorded the way a field notebook would: inked curves combed across the page, with one red thread running through. Click the piece for a new page.

title: Old Courses
note: An 1881 survey of a river that never flowed, thirteen channels deep. Click the piece for a new survey.

title: Overprint
note: Two ink passes over one quarter-circle grid: indigo first, rust second and a little off register, the way a tired press would lay it down. Click the piece for a new variation.

title: Strata
note: An imaginary terrain sliced like a museum model: translucent elevation layers floating in a dark studio, one warm layer among the ink blues. Drag to look around, click for a new landscape.

title: Tangency
note: A circle-packing study. Discs are placed largest first and grown until each touches a neighbor, so every circle is tangent to something. Rings and arc segments in rust, ochre, and slate on warm paper. Click for a new variation.

title: Lichtenberg
note: A crystal grown from static. Thousands of sparks drift in out of the dark and freeze the instant they touch the tree. Nothing here was drawn, only accreted. Click to grow a new one.

title: Kindling
note: Two fractal flames built from pure density, drifting into each other and back. Bright cores dissolving into smoke. Click for a new burn.

title: Kaleid 99
note: Oscillator bands through a ninety-nine-mirror kaleidoscope, thresholded into hard stripes and printed to near black on paper. One band of color keeps the rest honest. Click for a new variation.

title: Interruptions
note: A dense weave of short ink dashes, each the same length and turned at random, with whole regions erased back to paper. The holes are the drawing. Click for a new variation.

title: Storm Grid
note: Forty-nine nested squares drawn with a plotter's patience, except in two or three cells where the hand slipped. Click the piece for a new plot.

title: Feedback
note: One buffer of noise re-sampled through its own ghost until it settles into flowing grain. The settle is the event. Click the piece to run it again.

title: Long Shadows
note: Two to four vessels on a low table, drawn flat with long shadows and one accent pot per arrangement. The horizon never lands in the same place twice. Click the piece for a new seating.

title: Hour Hands
note: A clock that repaints itself every minute: three rings for seconds, minutes and hours, each a slow journey between two colors. Click the piece to hold a still.

title: Half-Moon Dots
note: A breathing dotted field crossed by a slowly rotating crescent. Dots that straddle the edge are drawn bisected, so the boundary itself is the subject.

title: What Isn't There
note: A poster printed in reverse: every word exists only as erasure, carved, rubbed and punched out of the ink. Read the gaps.

title: Off Register
note: A playable print-shop instrument: twelve one-gesture motifs on keys A to L, each printed twice with a ghost-ink offset like the sheet slipped. Tap on mobile.

title: Tone Rows
note: A polargraph density study: vertical ticks drawn row by row, length following tone, whites lifting the pen. A rose window in machine handwriting.

title: Orbit Portraits
note: Strange attractors rendered like flame fractals. Every roll picks an orbit; a laciness test hangs the keepers and stamps the duds on the reject wall.

title: Half a Million Grains
note: Half a million grains of sandpaint falling one by one. Nothing is drawn except dots, and the picture emerges. Click the paper for a burst.

title: Own Lines
note: Every stroke is built by hand from shaded triangles, width shaped by pressure, so the line keeps a brush's habits. One study per click: a wave, a heron, bamboo, a grass tuft.

title: Wind Bent
note: Concentric rings sampled through a wind field that pushes in every direction. Click for a fresh gust.

title: Almost Perfect
note: One pen, one line, never lifted: nested squares whose rotation drifts as the path goes in. It draws itself like a plotter. Click for a new hand.

title: Living Homage
note: After Albers, but the squares never sit still: one slow palette journey, sizes breathing out of phase. Click to mint a fresh journey.

title: Typewriter Weave
note: Struck one character at a time with a shaky hand. Up close it reads as typing; from across the room it reads as cloth.

title: Eye Garden
note: A garden of eye sprouts that watch your pointer go by, pupils widening, then settle back to sleep. Sweep through it.

title: Greedy Squiggle
note: A plotter pen hunts the darkest pixel left on the page, erasing as it goes, lifting to relocate. Mostly one line.

title: Value Ramp Grid
note: Half-square triangles in a deliberate diagonal gradient, light to dark. Nothing else.

title: Bleed Ledger
note: Three hands negotiate on a ruled ledger: hidden pigment, pitted wounds, gravity-drawn streaks. Every trail reads back to its wound.

title: Fifty-Three Divisions
note: The octave divided into 53 commas, brass seams and all. Hover to read each comma in cents.

title: Hover
note: Marks breathing at the edge of visibility. Your pointer steadies them.

title: Retune
note: Two offset circle grids plus a sheared dot grid. Drag to retune and watch the moire re-resolve.

title: Convergence
note: A tilted crystal of 5-limit harmony. Pulses converge on the root and bloom on arrival.

title: Trough Walk
note: An octave as a washboard of tuning valleys. The probe snaps into troughs; wide ratios eat narrow ones.

title: Held and Shaped
note: Two panels, one material: pulse holds while color shapes, then they trade jobs every 24 seconds.

title: Prime Petals
note: A rosette in prime-numbered hues only. Each prime family grows exactly p petals.

title: Tritave Rose
note: Structure repeating at 3x instead of 2x: thirteen rings, marks sized by consonance, slow revolution.

title: Ten Times Exact
note: One recording played ten times byte-identically while the picture turns into notation. Your ears flip before your eyes do.

title: Seventeen Microns
note: A slider for droplet size against a fixed updraft. Find by eye where float becomes rain.

title: Hue Bingo Canvas
note: Every visit rolls a fresh Hue Bingo palette and lays it down as wobbling colour rings. Coherent by construction.

title: Standing-Wave Hatch
note: A hatch field where a sine wave decides how long each dash gets. Blades of darkness swim through the lines.

title: Family of Blobs
note: The same blob built four ways: harmonic, grown, contoured, implicit. One ink, one plate, the comparison is the picture.

title: Spiral Zap
note: One quiet triadic palette spiralled ten times, calm on the left and feral on the right. The tipping point is visible.

title: Budget Ink
note: A still life shaded on a strict ink budget.

title: Never Isles
note: A procedural antique nautical chart: radial-noise archipelago engraved as a maritime plate, with rhumb lines, twin compass roses, hachured relief, and recombined place-names. Click for a new chart.

title: Dissent
note: A grid of squares, each disobeying a little; a few burn vermilion. Click for another desordres.

title: Chord Orbits
note: Three rings of points joined every k-th pair by hairlines; one weaves a web, another a slow star. Click for new orbits.

title: Contour Drift
note: Sixty horizontal lines displaced by drifting noise; topographic calm in one ink. Click for a new drift.

title: Night Water
note: Blue-teal motes drift and breathe in dark water; a few wear faint rings. Click for a new tide.

title: Seven Moods
note: Seven palettes merging tones across eras and moods, 160 pieces adrift. Click for the next mood.

title: The Unwanted Visitor
note: A pink tray of pale water holds seven dahlia heads while a small yellow toy drifts at the edge. Watch only. The toy drifts in on its own schedule.

title: Leaking Light
note: Bare trees stand in red-orange fog while a blown-out leak eats the left edge. Drag to pull the light leak across the frame.

title: Britain in Colour, Pointed and Shot
note: Twelve vernacular prints in a fixed diary order, grain and date stamps included. Tap to turn to the next print.

title: Built Around the Crack
note: Four adults crammed in a miniature blue bedroom under a glowing ceiling crack. Drag to tilt the room. Release to let it settle.

title: The Lonely Bench
note: Three figures sit like furniture in a drab institutional room; one leans, glacially. Watch only. Nothing hurries here.

title: Oil Slick Gull
note: An oil-coated figure emerges from total darkness, found by cold highlights. Watch the sheen find the figure, then lose it.

title: The Column, Pt. 2
note: A rock-coloured figure crouches in sea spray under a pulsing gold halo. Watch the spray burst and the halo answer.

title: Two Passes, Same Hand
note: A night shore grades itself from near-black to deep blue to hot ember. Drag to pull the grade from black to ember.

title: The Room's Own Light
note: Four figures in a church hall under warm tungsten light. Watch the room breathe.

title: The Wash Does the Story
note: A staged interior flattened into a single deep-blue wash. Tap to re-light the room.

title: One Eye Stays Sharp
note: A face seen through rippled water, one blue eye perfectly sharp. Drag to tilt the water.

title: Exposed for the Force
note: A towering smoke column churns at sunset above a tiny hooded figure. Watch the column churn.

title: As the Element
note: A reclined figure rendered as one dark mass, wet sheen the only anatomy. Drag the light across the body.

title: Set Piece
note: A smoke column rises at sunset while a small watcher crouches, utterly still. Watch the light fade.

title: Elevated Snapshot
note: Three found arrangements from straight overhead: a bin, a sheep, a televised match. Tap for the next snapshot.

title: The Shadow In Frame
note: An overhead portrait in still water, the photographer's own shadow crossing the frame. Drag to move the light.

title: Night Shelter
note: A crowd under a bus shelter, flash firing, a giant ad glowing behind them. Watch for the flash.

title: The Bread Session
note: A deadpan listener crouches before a loaf of bread wired into headphones. Tap to re-stage the set.

title: Caustics
note: Sunlight draws bright caustic lines across a submerged body in green water. Watch the light move.

title: One Hard Source
note: Figures cross one hard light in the dark, flaring the frame toward white. Watch the light.

title: The Zenith Body
note: A figure holds still in green water as foam drifts and the photographer's shadow crosses below. Drag to tilt the camera.

title: Burn and Stamp
note: A monochrome landscape builds, burns to white, and is signed in hot pink. Drag to push the exposure.

title: Infinite Strangers
note: Twelve tiny cities in parallel, pianos and umbrellas falling from the sky, and a narration that advances one clause at a time. Watch the skies.

title: Hyper-Real
note: One figure in two rooms: alone she composes toward a form that never lands, together she plays inside warm moving light, and the black gutter between them holds. Watch both rooms.

title: Scene 1: Preface
note: A hand-bound book: Narrator and Chorus alternate while the room behind the words shifts. Tap to turn the page.

title: Small Figure, Huge Sea
note: A vast monochrome sea does everything; one tiny figure raises an arm against the scale. Watch the tides.

title: Adumbration
note: A slow dark sub field and a bright granular field hold their opposition, never resolving. Drag to lean toward a pole.

title: Prose Before Lyric
note: Prose types itself, and each finished sentence frees a melodic line. Watch the prose become lyric.

title: The White Whale
note: A golden form almost finishes, then unravels, leaving one thin white line. Drag to chase it.

title: Green Room, 4-Track

title: The Turning Away
note: Dark field with a rigid system on the left: a row of tall, even bars, all the same height and color, ticking up and down in lockstep. On the right, a loose circle of dots dances, varied sizes, varied speeds, warm colors. A slow band of light drifts left to right; wherever it passes over the bars, they soften: they bend, shorten, warm in color, and drift toward the circle, joining its dance. When the band passes, the bars firm up again, but one bar each cycle stays soft and stays with the circle. 240 s super-loop = 4 cycles x 60 s; converts accumulate within the super-loop (1 bar soft at end of cycle 1, 2 at end of cycle 2, 3, then 4) and reset only at the super-loop boundary. Dragging along the band holds it in place; dragging a bar toward the circle converts it early. Probes (46/46): converts accumulate exactly and all bars are rigid again at t=240; loop closure byte-identical; band monotonic over 0-50 s, centered at t=30, reset at t=60; a bar under the band is soft, shorter, tilted, warmed, drifted right; band drag freezes and resumes exactly, never freezes permanently; bar drag converts exactly that bar early and it stays soft into later cycles; drag away converts nothing; all 9 dots still dance at t=200-202, the circle never turns rigid. Fix rounds (1): the first build latched converts per cycle only, so a convert firmed up again when the next cycle started, contradicting the prompt's latched convert; the fix accumulates converts within the super-loop and resets only at its boundary, with converts made distinct (raw seeded draws repeated bar 0 twice, so the draw now picks an index into the not-yet-converted bars, same seed and draw positions, so all later seeded values are untouched). Readings: a bar-drag convert is keyed to the current band-cycle; the light band is drawn behind the bars as a flat translucent rect.

title: Atoms From Then to Now
note: Frame split by a faint vertical seam into a then side (left, dimmer, cooler) and a now side (right, warmer, brighter). Small particles drift slowly left to right; as each one crosses the seam, it changes: cooler and smaller on the left, warmer and larger on the right, with a brief bright flash exactly at the crossing. Particles never rush; the seam never moves; the two sides never mix. 240 s loop: each particle completes an integer number of traversals per loop at 3, 6, or 9 px/s at 720 wide; crossed particles fade over the far right and reappear on the left as cool particles. Dragging on a particle hurries its crossing; dragging on the seam bends it slightly (particles crossing near the bend shift their path, the seam springs back). Probes (25/25): loop closure byte-identical; particle 0 drifts left to right monotonically with no reversal; left-side particle cool slate at base radius, right-side particle warm at 1.6x radius; flash above 0.7 within 0.002 of the seam and below 0.05 beyond 0.05; crossed particle fades in u (0.88, 0.96), invisible past u = 0.985, reappears cool on the left after wrap; seam x and effective seam constant without drags; particle drag hurries the crossing, leaves other particles exactly untouched, resumes schedule exactly after release + ease-back, never reverses flow; seam drag bends by the drag delta, shifts only nearby crossing paths, springs back to zero after release. Reading: hurries its crossing is realized as a 3x clock while the particle is held (the pointer need not steer the particle's position); the particle still follows its own path, only faster.

title: The Gathering, Not the Masterpiece
note: Wide dark field with a loose circle of small marks (dots, short bars, tiny rings), each in its own muted color, facing inward. The marks exchange properties on contact: when two marks drift near each other, one hands the other its color or its rhythm, and the giver takes on a new one from the pool. No mark keeps a property for long; the circle's overall palette drifts slowly over minutes, never settling, never repeating exactly. 300 s loop: 12 marks orbit at 1-2 revolutions per loop, 29 precomputed proximity exchanges from scanning the fixed orbits at 0.25 s steps with a re-arm margin; each exchange swaps exactly one property (color, shape, or pulse-rate rhythm) with a 1.2 s pale flash at the pair midpoint. Dragging a mark toward another fires that pair's exchange at once; dragging a mark out of the circle returns it on release via a 2 s smoothstep glide; drag never fixes a color, never stops the drift, never adds a mark. Probes: loop closure byte-identical; all three shape kinds present; all marks drift over 60 s; no mark within 0.25 units of center; radii varied; sampled event groups occur on proximity, change only their own pairs with one property type each, with correct swap relations and a brightened flash disc at the midpoint; palette histogram drifts across the loop; toward-mark drag records and applies that pair's exchange vs a control instance; out-of-circle drag returns within 2.5 s of release and stays on orbit; held marks still change color at scheduled events; other marks keep drifting while one is held; count stays 12. Readings: never repeating exactly is realized within each 300 s loop (palette drifts without settling across the loop); across loops the sequence restarts exactly, the film-loop restart used by sibling pieces, required by the byte gate. Rhythm means the mark's pulse rate (breathing scale oscillation), not its orbital speed, so the precomputed proximity schedule stays exact after rhythm exchanges.

title: Fifty-Two Weeks
note: Grid of 52 small tiles (13 columns by 4 rows), each holding one tiny scene: a dot, a bar pair, a ring, a zigzag, a pulse. The tiles fill with color one at a time, week by week, left to right, top to bottom; a filled tile keeps its scene but glows softly. When all 52 fill, the grid holds for a beat, then empties in reverse order, one tile at a time, and the year starts again. The tone is warm and wry: colors shift slightly warmer as the year fills, cooler as it empties. 322 s loop: fill 0-156 s (one tile every 3 s), hold 156-166 s, empty 166-322 s in exact reverse order. Drag stir: pointer drags record samples; each bead's offset is a closed-form sum over samples within 8 s (radial push, Gaussian falloff σ 70 px, exponential settle τ 2.5 s, capped at 40 px); no tap action, never click-to-reload. The prompt's WebGL spec is canvas 2D (QA renderer has no WebGL) — beads as flat ellipse fills, portrait as a seeded analytic brightness function (dark hair ellipse, lighter face ellipse, shoulder ellipse, feathered edges), never a photo, real face, or likeness; no offscreen canvas, gradients, shadowBlur, Path2D, createElement, or AudioContext. Probe harness driving the piece's own pointer listeners: a drag at t=1 s changes 132,790 px at t=1.5 s (beads visibly shoved aside along the drag path, opening a gap in the face oval); at t=9 s only an exponential-tail residue remains; at t=12 s the dragged run is pixel-identical (0 differing px) to the undisturbed run — the stir fully settles.

title: Kinetic Scroll
note: A landscape plywood frame on dark ground, with a flat-alpha soft shadow and nothing else outside it. Left third: three vertical etched-acrylic panels at 40% alpha carrying seeded hatch lines and abstract etched marks (arcs, dashes, dots — never letterforms). Right two-thirds: the cotton scroll with three horizontal pigment stripe rows (indigo, rust, moss top to bottom, with seeded variation and grain). A crimson basting thread runs in a long sine curve from the scroll's rolled left edge to the needle station at about 55% of the scroll width — stitched partway, as specced — with the needle drawn as a slanted line plus thread-colored dot. Mobile keeps the same landscape composition as a centered band. Motor: each pointermove event contributes a capped displacement (±90 scroll-px); offset(t) = 320 + sum dx_i·(1 − exp(−(t − t_i)/0.35)), so the scroll eases in after movement and settles as the exponentials saturate — never frame-integrated state; idle > 2 s: needle parks (angle relaxes from −0.35 to 0.15 rad). Endless scroll: content is never stored — segment (row, k) is a pure seeded function of scroll-space position (260 px segments, home-pigment rows with 25% seeded cross-pigment variation, grain, accent slivers), so revealed sections recycle as new seeded bands ahead. Thread: dashes live in scroll-space (26 px dash / 14 px gap), so stitches travel with the cloth; the needle station at 55% of scroll width stitches cloth as it feeds past. TAP (under 12 px movement): cycles thread color crimson → indigo → moss → crimson. Bands drawn procedurally per frame from seeded segment functions (no band buffer, no offscreen canvas); all tones flat-alpha, no gradients, no shadowBlur; soft shadow as one flat-alpha offset rect. Probe harness driving the piece's own pointer listeners through its rAF loop: frame one → 1 s of pointer travel changes 244,496 px (scroll feeding); 1 s → 4 s changes 30,736 px (still easing); 4 s → 8 s idle changes 0 px by more than 4/255 per channel (2,459 edge pixels differ by ≤4 — antialiasing rounding on the exponential tail, visually stopped); a tap after settling changes 1,975 px, confined to the thread/needle (crimson → indigo). No readable text except the title.

title: Red Stage
note: An open public platform at dusk, shot from slightly above, full-bleed. Dusk sky in layered flat-alpha bands from deep dusk blue-violet at top to warm dusk brown at the horizon, with one strong dusk light source — a warm layered glow near the horizon that slowly shifts (60 s sine on alpha, 90 s sine on position). Below, a plaza stone field with faint seeded joint lines and a dusk shadow wash. At center, a simple red-painted stage in canvas pseudo-3D — trapezoid top surface over a front face, flat-alpha cast shadow down-right. On the stage, left to right: a chrome microphone stand, a stack of three dark-cloth books, a wood stool, and a clay pot with green leaves. Around the plaza periphery, faint ghost crowd figures drift on slow sines — peripheral and ghostly, never the subject. The stage is EMPTY at loop start: every presence must arrive through interaction. Idle: the stage sits empty and the dusk light slowly shifts; the crowd drifts; nothing else happens. No autoplay, no sound of any kind (no applause sound). Touch the stage: an activator appears — a dark silhouette sprite performing a small gesture loop on a 3.2 s cycle (4 frames at 0.8 s each): raises a book, plays a silent instrument, dances two steps, or reads; gesture order advances in a fixed seeded sequence, never random; each activator fades in over 1 s, gestures for 20 s total, fades out over the last 3 s, then dissolves back into the crowd. Cap: up to 6 activators share the stage, each in its own stage slot on its own gesture loop; when a 7th touch arrives, the oldest still-standing activator dissolves over 2 s; a dissolving activator vacates its slot for the newcomer. The stage never empties itself and never reloads — only the viewer adds. Drag pans the plaza view (closed-form decay, tau 2.5 s after release, clamped to plus-or-minus 40 px horizontal / plus-or-minus 24 px vertical); a drag never adds an activator, only a tap (movement under 12 px) on the stage rect does.

title: The Heart Balloon
note: A monochrome, slightly grainy doorbell-camera frame — wall above, driveway below, faint wall seams and driveway joints, flat-alpha vignette bands, a faint gray REC corner mark with blinking dot. The dark trunk sits lower-center, tilted about minus-three degrees, with a thin light strip along its top edge. Five gray blob-boxes and one standing cylinder cluster at the trunk. The pink heart balloon sits above the trunk's left-center, tethered by a light-gray string to the cluster, with a small pink reflection ellipse on the trunk below it. The pink is the only color in the scene. Watch-only, sixty-second loop: zero to about forty seconds hauling — objects shift on small sine jitters while the balloon stays tethered, string swaying; escape at a seeded moment (cycle zero: thirty-nine-point-five-nine seconds; each cycle reseeds, giving thirty-eight to forty-two seconds): the string detaches and dangles from the balloon; rise, fifteen seconds: ease-out ascent with slight sine sway, drifting up and off-frame; the pink trunk reflection fades as the balloon climbs; fifty-seven to sixty seconds: reset crossfade on the main canvas — the next cycle's frame one fades in over the current scene. The balloon never pops or bursts; it escapes, it doesn't die. Film grain is a closed-form seeded function of the quantized time index, never per-frame random. A tender surveillance-footage moment abstracted — exactly one intrusion.

title: Right Here, Right Now
note: A soft gallery-white wall holding four lines of dense matte graphite, formally restrained, centered, generous margins, each line about sixty percent of field width, stacked with wide leading and faint pencil guide rules beneath — RIGHT HERE, / RIGHT NOW, / EVERYTHING, / FOREVER in canonical order. Graphite texture reads as hand-brushed (three offset passes per glyph at varying alpha plus speckle dots), not crisp vector type. Exactly one intrusion: a single rhinestone glint embedded in the counter of the R in RIGHT NOW, pulsing slowly — verified by a gold-pixel scan of the shipped thumb: exactly one glint cluster (seven gold-ish pixels in a single two-by-four-pixel box). Watch-only, two-hundred-forty-six-second cycle: each line draws itself over about forty-five seconds, characters accumulating left to right with visible brush texture; the full wall then holds sixty seconds with only the rhinestone glinting; a soft six-second wipe fades the wall back to blank paper, then the next cycle begins with a newly seeded word order (cycle zero keeps the canonical order; later cycles shuffle via seeded random). Frame one is phase-shifted to open in the hold phase (all four lines complete), per the hold-phase precedent — the draw mechanic still runs every cycle. Formally restrained yet conceptually expansive — the graphite carries the only weight in the room.

title: How to Fly (ombré)
note: A mural-scale ombré field, pink at top through gold in the middle to teal at the bottom, smooth with no banding. Eight white-bordered photo-rects float at three scale tiers with generous air: two large prints (birthday-cake glyph, car glyph), three medium (book, plant fronds, cake), three small (plant, book, car). Glyphs are clean outlines, never photographic, never faces. The book glyphs carry the prompt-specced spine label JAZZ, legible on both. Rhinestone glints and gold glitter drift between the rects. Watch-only slow drift: rects bob on independent phases (nine-to-sixteen-second periods, six-to-sixteen-pixel amplitude), glitter drifts upward on a closed-form wrap, rhinestones glint on a slow traveling sine wave. Drag gently pans the whole mural (recorded segments decaying with tau two-point-five seconds, clamped to plus-or-minus forty pixels horizontal and plus-or-minus thirty vertical); the photos keep their relative drift under the pan. The ombré is ninety layered flat-alpha horizontal bands, never a gradient; the small tier is widened from six percent to eleven percent of field width on narrow fields so glyphs stay legible on phones. Family-archive stand-ins against an ombré rainbow backdrop — glitter, rhinestones, cars, and plant life.

title: DOTS (instruction no. 1)
note: A square twelve-by-twelve dot grid on paper with generous margins, faint stencil grid lines underlying everything, cool-gray offset shadows (forty percent alpha) making each dot hover slightly above the paper. Frame one opens mid-build (phase-shifted twelve seconds, per the hold-phase precedent): most PRIMARY-palette dots filled, the last seeded cells still empty or mid-fill as pale discs, and the single half-moon hack already visible (row eleven, column four, blue). Thirty-six-second cycle: twenty-four seconds layer-by-layer build (each cell starts on a zero-point-fifteen-second stagger in seeded order, fills over two seconds in three flat-alpha pencil passes plus faint chord strokes for pencil texture), eight seconds hold, four seconds crossfade to the next predetermined palette (PRIMARY to RAINBOW to BLACK-AND-WHITE, cycling). Exactly one hack per cycle: one seeded cell breaks into a half-moon at a seeded angle, verified by a forced-time hold-phase probe showing the complete grid with exactly one half-moon. Double-tap reseeds the pattern and jumps to a seeded random palette; a single tap never reloads. No viewer drawing, no freeform scatter, no palettes outside the three predetermined sets, no gradients inside dots. Pure instruction art — a RULE, the grid is the point, openly in the Sol LeWitt conceptual lineage.

title: Drawing as Incantation
note: Blank paper at frame one — the drawing begins at load, so the gate holds. Watch-only, two-hundred-six-second cycle: strokes accumulate over one-hundred-eighty seconds in seeded order — paper flecks, faint margin grid, page border, twenty-six typewriter lines of dash, dot, and tick glyphs, a hatched redaction bar over one line, then a flowing signature scrawl in the lower third (single polyline with loops that return to the path, crossing flourishes, underline). At completion, exactly one action: a single purple spray-paint line strikes diagonally through the signature over one second (progress-gated core polyline plus five-hundred-twenty seeded spray particles, the hiss drift). Hold twenty seconds, crossfade to paper over five seconds via main-canvas alpha overlay (no offscreen canvas), then a newly-seeded page begins. No viewer input at all. The signature is never a legible real name; smooth vector strokes forbidden — the hand reads in the texture. Drawing as incantation, cast for healing and real justice.

title: The Dossier Wall
note: A gallery wall covered floor-to-ceiling with a ten-by-six grid of off-white dossier pages mounted on a glowing neon-pink plexiglas substrate, darkened at the edges. Each page carries pseudo-type lines (short gray dashes, never readable prose), one-to-three black redaction bars each drawn over a text block it obscures, and — on about sixty percent of pages — a stylized signature scrawl that is never a real name. Three handwritten margin notes carry the only legible words, verbatim from the prompt: HOW DO WE GET FREE?, HERE, NOW. Over the wall: a hot-pink spray-mist field biased to the left third, and gold rhinestone glints clustered near page corners like constellations. Watch-only, one-hundred-twenty-second loop: the grid pans laterally on a sine (ping-pong, so the loop never jumps), as if the camera is reading the wall; rhinestones glint on a sinusoidal pulse plus a traveling light wave sweeping the wall every fourteen seconds; spray mist slowly re-settles, each blob drifting on its own slow sine phase and breathing in alpha. Double-tap reseeds the page layout and rhinestone positions; a single tap never reloads. The pink plexi substrate is layered flat alpha shapes, not a gradient. Hostile state documents flipped and re-appropriated with pink spray and rhinestones — glitter as transcendence, escape, and survival.

title: Three Windows
note: A square staged stack on a shellac floor filling the field — floorboards with grain lines, knots, and plank seams. The worn document page sits central at seventy percent, rotated four degrees, with a folded top-left corner, jagged torn right edge, abstract ink scrawl doodles, and a headline band of dash marks half-obscured by an ink blotch — no readable words. The snapshot sits on it at twenty-eight percent of field area, rotated minus-seven degrees from the document, white border, faded image of coral and denim blobs on sage, a pearl-dot arc, and an abstract grill grid — no faces, no real photo. The single hack reads clearly: the snapshot's top-right corner lifts and curls with its own cast shadow and highlight streak. Shadows are layered flat-alpha shapes, so the stack reads as physical staging, not a flat collage. Watch-only, ninety-second loop: a soft raking light band sweeps across the stack once, shadows shifting direction as it moves; the curled corner flutters once mid-loop and settles. Nothing else moves — a slow read. One hack only, every layer a window repeated in succession.

title: Broadcast Slices
note: The locked portrait — kitchen-white field, an abstract seated figure with chrome headphones at a chrome counter (head ellipse, headphone band and ear cups, trapezoid torso, one arm reaching, amber cup on the counter), seeded bottle rows in green, amber, and chrome at both edges, and nine abstract stamp glyphs — diamond, ring, star, cross, bar — floating in the upper third, no readable words, no likeness. The forty strips show as thin gaps even when locked, so the slice structure reads from the first frame. Watch-only, forty-second loop: six seconds locked, eighteen seconds drifting out of sync on per-strip seeded amplitude, phase, and speed, eight seconds re-locking, eight seconds holding; three seeded strips per loop flip mirrored and stay flipped until the loop boundary. Drag scrubs the slice-offset field, decaying back after release — a system to explore the collage's permutations. The portrait is readable only when the strips lock; most of the time they drift out of sync.

title: Tent for Close Readings
note: The viewer inside a shamiana: six block-printed cotton panels in madder red, indigo, and cream radiating from an implied apex above the top edge, filling the whole frame with no outside visible — each panel its own print-and-dye combination of diamonds, triangles, dots, and rings, the two center panels carrying the strongest motif, side panels fading toward the edges, dashed stitch lines along the panel edges with gold beading dots on beaded panels. Slow watch-only drift: the panels breathe on long sines and the light through the cloth strengthens and dims in long cycles; a gentle pointer drag pans the view slightly inside the tent with depth-scaled parallax between panel layers. No tent poles, no structure, no people, no sky — the cloth is the architecture, panels lifted off the block printer's table and simply hung in the sky.

title: Rabari Embroidery
note: A deep indigo achadiya field, full-bleed, with soft pale ghost washes and faint ghost block motifs beneath — and bright Dhebariya Rabari embroidery creeping across it in bands on gentle diagonals: chain stitches in orange, pink, and green forming mirror-centered rosettes and zigzag bands, plus buttonhole-edged patches, each band visibly detouring around the palest ghost areas rather than crossing them, forcing a more careful reading of the cloth beneath. Five seeded mirror rosettes sit along the bands, each a small mirror center with ten radiating chain stitches. Embroidery covers well under forty percent; the indigo shows. Drag to embroider: a needle-following stitch line extends from the last rosette toward the pointer, laying chain stitches, the thread color cycling per rosette; double-tap places a mirror rosette; mirrors glint on pointer pass. Watch-only otherwise — nothing happens without the drag. No symmetrical mandalas, no neon threads: motifs cluster and wander like hand embroidery.

title: The Block Carver's Table
note: A woodblock seen face-on at left in warm teak with wavy stylized grain, bevel highlights, and a depth side — its ajrakh rosette carved in reverse, recessed dark outlines with cut-highlight ticks — beside a thin vertical rule and the print it produced at right in black on cream, showing the same motif correct-reading with three mis-registered impressions fading down-right and registration crosshairs at the corners, a faint blue grid behind everything. Watch-only: the block rests, a roller pass inks its face, it stamps with a small lift, the ink starves a little with each stamp, and mid-loop one petal groove deepens as the carver re-carves it. The motif is seeded once for the whole piece, so block and print always agree — the print shows the same motif, as the process demands. Stylized drawn wood, no literal hand: the hand is implied through the stamp action.

title: She Arose
note: A circular pool fills the frame edge to edge on deep plum ground — concentric rings of braided worn-sari ropes in cobalt, magenta, marigold, and ivory, crossing and interweaving, trailing off beyond the frame, no floor line. At its center the dancer exists only as braid density: nine interweaving near-vertical braids, two fanning bundles raised like arms, a small tangle of partial loops where a head would be. Remove the density and there is no figure at all. The braid field breathes on a slow sine; drag upward and she rises, braids streaming downward like hair in water; drag downward and she sinks, braids gathering. No literal body, no face. A state of becoming.

title: Kala Pani
note: A square panel of aged paper: an invented colonial engraving in crosshatch lines and ornamental borders, faded ink on tea-stained ground — a three-arch colonnade, a domed pavilion, diamond motifs, corner rosettes, no real print copied anywhere. Over it, embroidery: floral vines and a female face stitched in marigold, deep green, and crimson floss, denser where the architecture sits, the thread curves partially obscuring the print beneath. On load the engraving fades in first, then the embroidery stitches over it; drag over a stitched region and the stitches lift slightly, then settle. Stand still and the engraving dims, leaving the thread as the lasting image. Brown reclamation: the stitch outlasts the print.

title: Complex Silence
note: A nine-foot microphone looms in a dark room, and it only whispers. Sixteen seeded text fragments — half-translated memories, self-reflection shards — rise from the grille on slow cycles, bone-italic: I left my name at the airport; the rain in Seoul smells like home. The response is inverted and never explained: tap near the mic and it hushes, fragments thinning and scattering; stand still five seconds and the soundscape swells, fragments multiplying, the mic swaying. No volume control, no meter, no loud payoff. The instrument of amplification, nine feet tall, that refuses to amplify.

title: Theater of the Mind
note: Two eyes in the dark, cropped tight, and nothing else. They look left, and behind them a doorway you can barely see brightens; they look up, and a hand-shaped ghost stirs. The story plays out in the theater of the mind, synced to the gaze — fixation, saccade, blink. Drag, and the piece looks where you pull. Tap, and it blinks for two full seconds of pure black.

title: Greeting Algorithm
note: A small soft-bodied someone crosses a pale desert to greet a saguaro: it leans its whole body against the cactus and holds the hug for half a minute. Then it goes to the boulder and lies along its slope, mirroring the angle. Then back to the cactus. Greeting, not conquering — it never climbs, never plants anything, and it has no face. Each greeting lasts as long as it lasts.

title: Held Empty Frame
note: The camera holds an empty golden-hour field — low sun, one tree, long shadows — for forty seconds of almost nothing: a heat shimmer, a single blade of grass twitching. Then a small figure crosses the whole frame, leans against the tree for a while, and leaves. The field returns to stillness, and holds again. What happens when nothing happens is the piece. Tap to skip ahead to the entrance.

title: Scream but Not Cry
note: A white flag burning on the Racetrack Playa. The burn line crawls up the cloth; press and hold to scream, and the flame grows, the embers lift, the flag whips harder — and nothing else changes. The rocks keep their faint trails until the rain comes and erases them, on schedule, whether you screamed or not. Screaming only consumes the flag faster. That is the whole piece, and it has no text in it at all.

title: Smoke (Four-Colour Catastrophe)
note: After Supnet's Smoke: an ink volcanic plume on paper that you zoom into until the image dissolves into its own printing — CMYK rosettes blooming at the edges, registration drifting apart, until at forty times there is no catastrophe left, only misregistered dots. Closeness dissolves it. Drag vertically to dive; double-tap to come back to the whole picture.

title: Windshield Baby
note: A street corner through a Gameboy Camera: 160 by 144 pixels, four greens, nothing else — not even the frame counter. Cars are blocks, faces are four-pixel smears, the camera re-exposes with a hard snap every few seconds and drops frames as it goes. Nothing happens, and the ordinariness is the dehumanization. Drag to pan in hard 8-pixel chunks.

title: The JPEG Decides
note: One text, three file formats. The US Constitution rendered as 48 flat bands whose colors are computed through a quantization table — and every 30 seconds the table changes: JPEG luminance gives blues and teals, chrominance gives magentas, DCT rounding gives warm reds. The plaque names the table. The hand is nowhere in it. Drag sideways to scrub between tables.

title: Windows into the Continuum
note: One jagged screech line, endlessly reprocessed: sped up, slowed, chopped, looped, fed back through itself, each process labeled as it lands. A scrubber marks "you are here" on a timeline with no start and no end. A window, not the work. Watch only.

title: Satromizer
note: A wrong tool for a calm landscape: five sliders (SMEAR, TEAR, CHANNEL, STUTTER, DECAY) each genuinely corrupt the picture in real time. Drag them; tap BYPASS to A/B clean against corrupted; double-tap a slider to zero it.

title: Basic Waveforms
note: Three neon waveforms march in their lanes over a dim burst field: the square wave's edges tear the field, the sine smears its channels, the sawtooth drops flat blocks — all stepped to a 120bpm beat. Watch only.

title: Hyperobject Acts
note: Climate grief in four acts over one dark scanline field — denial barely glitches, despair detonates into databend chaos, acceptance settles into rhythmic green bands, defiant hope locks into a rising yellow diagonal. Hard cuts only. Watch only.

title: Room Tone
note: Twelve invented glyphs rot left to right across a twelve-second loop, stems splitting into red fragments, while the small cyan reference row beneath stays perfectly legible — the computer still understands it. Watch only.

title: Favourite Songs
note: Sixteen imaginary songs, each drawn as its own binary data reinterpreted into pixels — noise fields, byte-run stripes, flat loud blocks, nothing like a waveform. One panel remixes itself at a new bit depth each cycle. Watch only.

title: Raw Import
note: A picture of flat tiles is imported as raw audio and run through an echo effect: the top rows stay clean as a header while every row below tears into ghost copies and channel splits — Roberts's 2009 Audacity databending tutorial. Watch only.

title: Unread Characters
note: Kimchi and Chips' unread characters: three hundred frosted lenses over a field of warm bokeh, and hidden in the light, one hand-written line, the crow's eye counts the unlit windows. Head-on there is nothing to read. Drag to tilt the panel and find the one angle where the dots become handwriting.

title: Optical Rail
note: Kimchi and Chips' optical rail: a warm back-lit print, hatching, halftone, three bold circles, one red band, that never moves at all. What moves is a train of glass lenses crossing it, bending the pattern only where they pass. The image is still; the seeing travels. Drag a lens; double-tap to reverse the rail.

title: 483 Lines
note: Kimchi and Chips' 483 lines: all 483 NTSC scanlines standing in a dark field like threads, bending in slow waves, brightening where they gather into folds. Every forty-five seconds a warm field sweeps down and the whole field re-tunes. Drag to pull a fold; tap to hold it.

title: Last Clock
note: Jussi Aengesleva's last clock, with Ross Cooper: no hands, no numbers, three rings of one-pixel slices from a small procedural sky, the last minute, the last hour, the last twelve hours, new slices bright, old ones fading to ghosts, until the face is a mandala of archived time. Drag to scrub the archive.

title: Terravision
note: Joachim Sauter's Terravision, the globe from 1994: a seeded planet tilted at twenty-three and a half degrees, mottled continents on deep ocean. Drag to spin it with momentum; scroll to dive from orbit to terrain to the warm grid of the cities.

title: Kinetic Rain
note: Joachim Sauter's kinetic rain: two fields of bronze droplets on invisible wires ripple through a twenty-five-second choreography of swells, peaks and spirals, brighter the higher they ride. Drag across the field to disturb it and watch the drops settle back.

title: Scroll Story
note: Markus Kison's scroll story: eight hundred particles on warm paper read an essay in four movements, stream, bars, scatter, rings, morphing as you scroll and retracing exactly when you scroll back, a one-line caption under each. Scroll, or let it read itself.

title: Scanlines
note: Markus Kison's scanlines: an abstract lathe-turned vessel turns slowly in the dark while a red laser line sweeps its height every twenty seconds, the surface resolved above the line and dissolving into drifting points below it. Drag to turn it yourself.

title: Finder of Wonders
note: Markus Kison's finder of wonders: the piece is a finder window, sidebar folders named DOTS, LINES, FIELDS and CURRENTS, each opening a live little world in the pane, with subfolders that vary it. Tap through the folders; the chrome is the frame, the worlds are real.

title: Live Miniature
note: Markus Kison's live miniature: a city block on a dark table whose faces carry tiny living feeds, people as dots inside lit windows, blinds sweeping, all slightly mis-registered at the corners, while a forty-second day turns gold to dusk to night. Drag to walk around it.

title: Four Particles Lost
note: Daniel Franke's four particles lost in honey: four plain bright particles drift a dark tank on a seventy-five-second loop, and their long teal ribbons, folded and layered, are the piece. Drag to stir the fluid and your wake will linger; double-tap to still the tank.

title: The Point Body
note: Daniel Franke's point body: fourteen thousand white points make a dancer in the black, depth-shaded and never still, while a closed-form sound score drives the camera, close and slow in the quiet passages, wide and fast in the loud ones. Tap to reseed, drag to take the camera, double-tap for a new dancer.

title: The Emotional Machine
note: onformative's doctrine as a machine: a shy blue particle nebula fills a dark room, and where the small bright visitor lingers, the field warms to violet and teal and gathers into slow spirals. Drag to be the visitor; leave, and it cools and forgets.

title: Watson's Halo
note: onformative's Watson identity: a dotted coral halo floats in a sterile white corridor while a swarm of coral, teal and peach dots drifts around it. Drag and the swarm gathers to your attention; let go and it relaxes back into itself.

title: The Inside-Out Sun
note: onformative's Anima Iki: a glowing sphere wrapped in green-violet liquid metal hangs in a purple-washed dark room, the only light there is. Drag near it and the fluid quickens and brightens toward you, the way it answered movement in the gallery.

title: Immaterial Terrain
note: onformative's Immaterials as a living contour map: a terrain of dense blue-white iso-lines breathes on black, ridges rising and collapsing as the noise field evolves, while every fifteen seconds a bright scan band sweeps across and redraws the lines it crosses. Watch only.

title: The Robot's Cue Sheet
note: Marco Tempest's robot cue sheet: a gray block-headed machine works through its poses, GREET to PRESENT to POINT, as a playhead sweeps six amber cues on the timeline below, its cyan face panel swapping patterns at each mark. Watch only.

title: Card Cosmos
note: Marco Tempest's card cosmos: a 52-card deck dealt one tap at a time into a calendar arc, each card an instrument with a season ring for its suit and a moon disc for its number, the active card floating large under cyan AR reticles. Tap to deal the next week.

title: The Conductor
note: Marco Tempest's master image: a lone conductor stands arms-raised in a white void while twelve black drones above him cycle through stack, ring and spiral on their own prearranged clock, orbs pulsing on one shared heartbeat. He commands nothing; the illusion is the piece. Watch only.

title: The Third Rail
note: Tatsuya Ishii's backstage rail: a small dark wall hangs from catenary cables under a ceiling rail, inching along at freight speed beside a grooved winch drum, while the motor drive unit blinks its one green LED. The machine before the performance. Watch only.

title: PolyNodes
note: Tatsuya Ishii's node network with a conductor: faceted polyhedra drift and re-knit in the dark while a magenta center node fires a pulse every six seconds, the wavefront reaching each node only after its per-edge delay. Watch only.

title: Reality / Delusion
note: Momoko Nishimoto's Cold Stares morph: one line-field rendered twice in the same frame, sharp white geometry for the real world and a warm grain-heavy double image for the delusion, crossfading with no cut. Drag sideways to hold the mix yourself; tap to rest at the shimmer midpoint.

title: Doors of Light
note: Architecture made of light: seven thin white rectangular frames hang in a black, misty room, nested like doorways and each turned a few degrees from the last. Small lens discs on fine wires are their sources. The frames breathe and swing slowly, never quite aligning. Drag near a frame to tilt its light plane around the lens. Tap to open one door in a brief bright flash.

title: Echo Vest
note: A haptic cloth rendered as the sensation, not the garment: on a near-black field, an unseen wearer drifts slowly, and rings of violet light radiate from them every second or so, thin and numerous, warming near the body and cooling to violet as they expand. A faint circle marks the edge of perception; when a ring crosses it, the ring brightens: the cloth sensing the room. Every so often the wearer stops and the rings tighten into a brief bright pulse, then release. One body listening to a dark room. Drag to become the wearer; hold still and the rings gather.

title: Layered Sequences
note: The mix is the composition: sixteen horizontal LED bars on black, and three light scripts running on them at once, additively. A cyan pulse train marches left to right; a magenta wave travels slowly; an amber swell breathes across the whole field. Where they overlap, the light whitens, and white happens nowhere else: no single script, and no pair, can reach it. The scripts never talk to each other; the beauty is accidental. Every thirty seconds the oldest script is swapped for a new behaviour and the piece keeps going. Double-tap to swap one now.

title: Sync Drift
note: Never lock, always chase: some two hundred small light nodes on a dark field, each running its own clock, wirelessly synced to one master beacon. Every twelve seconds the beacon fires and an alignment wave sweeps outward: nodes flare warm amber as it passes and snap toward the beacon phase, then drift takes them again, some lagging gray, a few lost entirely, packet loss and all. Alignment is a bright wave moving through a sea of stragglers. Drag to become radio interference and scramble the field locally. Double-tap to fire the beacon now.

title: Three Hundred and Ten
note: Scale as the piece: above a dark rooftop, a field of identical lighting modules hangs in the air, small domed shades glowing from within, receding in perspective until the count reads as endless: three hundred and ten of them, one light. The shades breathe in slow waves that travel across the field, warm and diffused, no beams, no spots. Occasionally one shade dims out of sequence, a faulty unit, honest, and re-syncs. Drag across the field to push a swell of brightness through it, a wind. Tap a shade to extinguish it until it re-syncs.

title: Sit Down, Move Through
note: Software that terminates in your body: you are strapped into a VR chair gliding slowly through a surrounding field of data: point clouds streaming past at true parallax speeds, cyan wireframe rings passing overhead, red detection-box constellations, deep blue washes behind. The viewpoint banks, rises, and dives on a slow heavy arc, and a faint chair outline at the bottom of the frame tilts with it: the machine you ride. The motion is a glide, never a thrill. Drag to steer the chair. Tap to commit to a dive or a rise.

title: Detect, Segment, Erase, Rebuild
note: A machine-vision pipeline played as an instrument: five horizontal stages show the same night street five ways. Detect: the scene with cyan boxes hunting two walking figures. Segment: the street reduced to flat coded masks, white people, magenta buildings, green road. Inpaint: the figures erased, the background visibly healing behind amber fronts. Depth: the scene as flat grays, near bright, far dark. Composite: the finished frame, counterfeit posters in the slots and glitch confined to the figures. A bright wave sweeps the stack, pulsing each stage as it passes.

title: Nine Buffers
note: A glitch composer as a playable artwork: a three-by-three grid of live buffers on black, each cell doing real work. Detection boxes hunt drifting targets; grayscale silhouettes wander; ad-slot masks appear and dissolve; a halftone field pulses; RGB noise chews a hidden figure; a depth wash shifts; flat segmentation blocks rearrange; a surface heals itself; and in the corner, the master cell composites them all. No labels, no numbers: the cells are the interface. Tap a cell to study it alone. Drag inside one to tune it.

title: A Face, In Dashes
note: Photographic content reduced to marks: on a black field, a giant face assembles from thousands of short white dashes, each one’s length set by the brightness of a generated portrait and its angle set by the portrait’s own contours. From a distance it is a face; up close it is only marks. It holds for a breath, dissolves back into scatter, and reassembles as a different face: frontal, three-quarter, profile, never the same twice. Thin green data columns scroll at the thirds behind it. Drag across it to scatter the assembly under your finger.

title: Before You Move
note: The signal arrives before the movement: a dozen braided pairs of lines flow across a dark field, a thin cyan signal line and a thicker white movement line tracing the same spikes and dives, the white always 120 milliseconds behind: you can see the future arriving. Where a signal spikes hard, a muscle-node flares and sounds: light and tone are triggered by the cause, never the effect. A tiny readout in the corner is proud of the head start. Tap to flex. Drag to draw a signal for the movement to chase.

title: 100 Agents, Straight Lines
note: The score, performed: one hundred agents walk in straight lines and nothing else. When two paths cross, both turn, left if the other is younger, right if older, and a white bloom marks the crossing. Their fading trails build a city: dense intersections downtown, long boulevards where nobody was interrupted. Every three minutes the score advances: the turn changes, the palette warms, the agents learn to avoid each other’s trails. Tap to freeze three agents mid-step. Drag to raise a temporary wall.

title: Weather Inside the Machine
note: The room responds: a latent-walk dreamscape whose weather is real. The hour sets its hue temperature (amber dawn, cyan noon, magenta dusk, deep blue night), the day of the year sets its turbulence, and a slow room-noise gives each day its own character. A thin strip at the bottom reads the room: the time, the drift, the calm. Open it at 6am and at 11pm and it is a different piece. Drag for a gust. No microphone: the room it reads is the clock’s.

title: Four Inks, One Poster
note: A poster printed the slow way, in the open: four halftone plates, cyan for temperature, magenta for visitors, yellow for words, black for time, each dot’s size a data value, each plate slightly misregistered, inks multiplying where they overlap. DATA IS A HUMAN MATERIAL, set big across the top. Tap to isolate one ink and read its stream alone, drag to push the registration out, double-tap for fresh data.

title: I Am a Piece. Ask Me Anything.
note: The companion narrator, and this one does not wait: it advances its own pages every seven seconds, measuring itself as it goes. Strips exactly as long as it claims, a width it can prove, a count of the babies born while you have been looking (it counted none of them). Drag it upward and it will tell you your altitude in anteater-tongues. Double-tap to slam it shut and hear something new.

title: I Am a Piece. I Am a Portal to the Data.
note: A book that narrates itself, strictly 1:1: it tells you its width in pixels and means it, keeps a water drop of exactly six pixels because a mouse drinks less than six millilitres a day, counts its own loop seconds while you stand inside them. No charts anywhere; the object is the data. Tap to turn its pages, drag to drop it and watch it splash exactly as wide as it is, double-tap to slam it shut and reopen it somewhere new.

title: Fused Grid
note: Four diamond quadrants of a circuit-board city, each tiled with random rectilinear street modules folded on themselves, hatched blocks scattered, two double-weight avenues crossing the whole. The plotter draws it quadrant by quadrant and the finished board stays. Drag to trace the streets with a fading current, tap to re-fuse a new city, double-tap for the black-on-white inversion.

title: Hilbert goes for a walk
note: A 16 by 16 grid walked by the Hilbert curve: squares bloom large and pale where the walk has just passed, settle through orange to red behind it, and wait ahead as small hollow outlines. Tap to re-roll the warm palette, drag to pull the walker to your finger, double-tap to subdivide into 32 by 32.

title: silly dither
note: A billowing volume made of nothing but white dots on black: ordered dithering, dense where the smoke is bright, dissolving at the edges. Drag to thicken the dots under your finger, tap to flip the dither pattern, double-tap to scatter it into static and watch it re-gather.

title: checkerboard fbm
note: A checkerboard warped by fbm noise into dark rolling terrain, lit like a storm: a bright blue-white front breaks in from one edge. Drag to move the light across the relief, tap to send the storm surging across the field, double-tap to flatten it to a perfect checkerboard for six seconds.

title: noise on top of noise
note: A pale pink wireframe torus, warped by noise on top of noise, tumbling slowly in a black void, small and alone. Drag to lean its spin, tap to reseed the warp, double-tap to freeze the noise away and see the perfect torus for six seconds.

title: The Board Is Listening
note: His statement as an instrument: systems that turn signals, joysticks, EEG, audio, into light and motion. Below, a dark panel with three labeled inputs, STICK, BRAIN, SOUND, each drawing its own live trace; above, one particle field, the light those signals become. Tap STICK and the field steers smoothly where the control points, with inertia. Tap BRAIN and the field stutters and blooms in erratic bursts, as if thinking. Tap SOUND and it pulses radially on a beat. Switching morphs the field's character over two seconds: one field, three nervous systems. Drag to feed the active input; draw wild zigzags into BRAIN for wilder bursts, circle steadily into SOUND for a steady pulse. Double-tap the field and all three argue at once. The traces never lie: they draw the actual control signals driving the light above them.

title: Until Observed
note: His first sketch, superposition: a particle in all its states at once until observed. A field of particles drifts in the void, each one rendered as a smear of four ghost positions, everywhere it could be, shimmering, never settling. Touch it and you become the observer: a collapse wavefront spreads outward from your finger at a visible speed, and particles it passes snap into single sharp white points, the field crystallizing into hard certainty around your hand.
