A tiny readout at the bottom names the state. Lift your finger and the certainty dissolves over a few seconds, the points smearing back into their ghost-clouds. Tap collapses one pinpoint star in the fog. Double-tap observes everything at once, two seconds of total sharpness, then full release into maybe. The collapse is beautiful, and it is also a loss: the sharp points are lonelier than the clouds.

title: 001 to 108
note: His spring discipline: 108 numbered daily sketches, and this is the sketchbook itself. One sketch fills the frame at a time, a small running system in the same monochrome hand, waveform, burst, matrix, osc, flock, pulse, and every twenty seconds the book advances: 001, 002, 003. The number and title sit at the top in amber, the only color, because the counting is the work; a thin rail along the bottom marks your place in the 108. Drag sideways to scrub through the book, the sketches playing live under your finger; tap to hold one and study it; double-tap to leap somewhere random. Every number is stable: sketch 015 always looks like sketch 015. Some are strong and some are duds, sparse little pixel and dot studies that barely move. The duds stay in. The lab keeps its failures, and that is its honesty.

title: Oscilloscope Music
note: The oscilloscope-music tradition, Fenderson's n-spheres: seven white spheres orbit a common center, their positions driven by two detuned oscillators, left channel as X, right channel as Y, so the sound is the picture. Their trails persist like phosphor, weaving rosettes, knots and near-circles that never quite repeat as the frequency ratio drifts in and out of phase near simple harmonics. The readout at the bottom tells you the ratio, because the number is the honesty. Drag horizontally to bend the ratio and warp the choreography, the drone you hear bending with it; drag vertically to offset the phase and knot the rosettes. Release and the ratio relaxes home toward a harmonic. Tap strikes a new shared phase; double-tap locks the ratio for a perfect ten-second loop. Ear and eye stay locked because there is only one signal.

title: Hairball
note: His neuroscience, drawn by itself: a hundred nodes drift on slow orbits inside a slowly rotating tangled ball, edges forming and dissolving between whichever nodes drift within reach. At rest it is dim and quiet, grey on black, a brain thinking almost nothing. Touch it and you become the electrode: nodes near your finger fire hot white, and the firing propagates along the edges like a seizure wave before settling back to rest over a few seconds. Slow drags raise gentle local waves; fast drags raise cascades. Tap strikes a single node and its neighbors answer. Double-tap silences the whole network for a breath, then it wakes node by node. A small readout counts the firing; most of the time it reads almost zero, and that quiet is what makes a cascade matter.

title: Deep Inside the Board
note: "Listen to the whispers of ghosts deep inside my no-input mixing board." The screen is near-black: a faint hand-drawn circuit of deep-green feedback traces, and along them, tiny dim motes, the ghosts, drifting. You cannot quite see them until you touch, and the touch they want is the quietest one: drag slowly near a trace and its ghosts wake, brightening toward phosphor green, their whisper-tones rising to the edge of hearing. Move fast and you scare them: the trace goes dark and silent for a while. Tap gently and the nearest ghost answers alone. Double-tap and they all converge toward your point and glow together, a quiet choir, then disperse. Haste is punished and stillness rewarded; the discovery of this is the tutorial, and the tone is tenderness, not haunting.

title: Held Back
note: Her arc from Berserk to ghost-whispers, held in one mass. A dense coil of red filaments sits at the center of the black, a system entirely capable of violence, played at whisper volume. Drag and you build pressure: the coil tightens, brightens, begins to tremble, amber highlights sparking at the highest strain, the sound climbing toward a howl that is hard-capped and never arrives. Release, and the pressure bleeds off over a long exhale, the mass loosening into grey ghost shimmer that drifts outward and fades. Tap strikes one point of the coil, a brief red flare. Double-tap bleeds it to near-black and it slowly re-coils over twenty seconds, because the coil always re-forms. The explosion never happens. The restraint is the composition, and it is beautiful precisely because of what it refuses.

title: No Input
note: Her instrument: a mixing desk with its outputs patched into its inputs, nothing else connected. This field is the same: rivers of phosphor-green signal stream across desk black, depositing energy into the very field that steers them, feeding on themselves and nothing else. Sometimes the loop finds a stable tone, a slow breathing band of light; sometimes it howls, a burst of feedback red the system takes seconds, or half a minute, to tame. You never command it; you accompany it. Drag and your amber fader-line bends the loop for a moment, gaining up locally, late and in the system's own way, before the loop swallows your touch. Tap for one clean pulse and watch it recirculate for many seconds. Double-tap drains the loop toward silence, and it re-boots itself from its own noise floor. Nothing enters from outside, ever.

title: Recorded From Somewhere
note: The xianchang poetics: a documentary of where the piece is running. Six hundred small marks fill the frame edge to edge, dots and dashes whose density, warmth and drift come from the place itself: its ambient swell and lull, its slow day turning warm to cool and back. A loud bright hour and a quiet dark one look like different places, because they are. Nothing is labeled; there are no meters and no clocks, the place reads in the marks, and everything changes like weather, never like a switch. Watch it record. Drag to stir the recording into a slow swirl that settles. Tap for a collision, the Three Gorges boats translated to light. Double-tap reseeds the place. The shipped piece listens to a simulated room, because a gallery page asks for no microphone; the place it documents is the one it imagines, completely.

title: One Platform
note: The Ekholux track builder's promise, kept small: "BUILD. RIDE. ENJOY. Start with a single platform. Build it into your own insane route." A black void, one neon platform, one small yellow rider rolling on it under gravity. That is all you get, and it is enough to start. Tap to place more platforms, snapped to a loose grid with a slight tilt; drag and your hand becomes a gravity well, bending the rider's arc as it launches off edges and lands, hopefully, on your architecture. Its trail fades behind it; complete a circuit and the route's ghost stays in the dark. If the rider falls out of the world, it loops back to the last platform it touched: the route is a closed world and nothing is lost. Double-tap clears back to one platform. Yours is the only light in the void, so build it well.

title: The Static Stare
note: Warhol's Screen Test, 1966: four minutes, one shot, a face that does not blink. An original portrait fills the frame in high-contrast black and white, half of it fallen into shadow, eyes open and looking straight out at you. Almost nothing happens, and the almost is everything: a breath at half a percent, the shadow edge creeping a few pixels over minutes, a jaw that shifts once. Blinks are scheduled every twenty to forty seconds, and every time, the eyelids tense, tremble, and do not close. The eyes never close. Watching is the interaction; the discipline is the piece. Stay for the whole take. It can tell whether you did.

title: The Locked Groove
note: The last side of Metal Machine Music ends in a locked groove: a 1.8-second loop cut so the needle can never leave, the record's ending chosen as an eternity. This piece does the same. For twelve seconds a form gathers out of near-black, the White Light/White Heat ghost treatment: a faint effigy, crown, sockets, jaw, drawn just above black, with one highlight edge arriving last; you have to look twice to be sure it is there. Then it locks. The final gesture, a slow 1.8-second breath through the form's tones, repeats forever: no outro, no fade, no resolution, ever. A small infinity sign sits in the corner like the side-4 label. Watch-only. The piece is not stuck. It chose this.

title: Ostrich Tuning
note: Lou Reed before the Velvets, on a Pickwick novelty record: every string tuned to the same D, the "Ostrich" machine he shared with Cale. Six horizontal strings span a near-black field, all at one fundamental, micro-detuned by fractions, and where their waves interfere, slow silver shimmer bands slide along the strings. A thirty-second loop: the strike, the drift as the bands travel, the settle back toward unison, a soft fade, and the strike again. There is nothing to touch and nothing to bend; the tuning is the piece, exactly as Reed built it. No guitar, no neck, no hands, just the lines and their beating. Watch it long enough and the shimmer starts to feel like weather inside a single note.

title: Between the Strings
note: The "All Tomorrow's Parties" session trick: paper clips wedged between piano strings until the piano rings like a small orchestra. A set of horizontal strings spans an ivory field, all on one pitch, and clips fall slowly from above on the piece's own schedule. Each landing perturbs its string: a kink travels down the line, a metallic shimmer settles around the clip, and the forest of perturbations grows, capped at twenty-four clips so the ring stays delicate. Drag across the strings to place clips yourself and cluster them into metallic chords; double-tap brings the sweep hand, clearing them left to right until the strings are clean sine again. Tap starts the sound, a soft pluck per landing, one pitch class only, because the clips are timbre, not melody. Preparation, accumulation, clearing: the instrument is the process.

title: All Strings to One Note
note: The Ostrich tuning, from Cale's months in The Primitives with Lou Reed: every string tuned to the same note, the guitar as a unison machine. Forty-eight vertical strings fill the frame, all vibrating at one frequency in perfect lock, their summed displacement glowing as a bright band at the center. The only event the piece allows: one string at a time slips slightly sharp, twenty cents of tension marked by an ember dot at its peg, beats against the field, and is pulled back into unison. Never two. Drag bends the nearest string sharp with your own hand and lets it settle home on release; double-tap drops the whole bank a semitone together, the field's color shifting with it. No chord ever forms. It is unison, or it is a brief, corrected mistake. The discipline is almost audible.

title: Three-String Drone
note: Cale's master mechanism, built as an instrument you file yourself. In the Dream Syndicate he put a pickup on his viola and filed the bridge down, day after day for eighteen months, until the bow caught three strings at once. Here one beam spans the black, and one bright line rides it. Drag downward and you are filing: the line widens, separates into three detuned voices, white, smoke, amber, and the interference between them starts to beat and brighten, a melody rebuilt as a chordal drone. Drag up and it collapses back to a single string. The little pickup glyph rides the beam and glows with the total amplitude; the readout at the bottom is the luthier's caliper, bridge height in millimetres. Tap to start the sound; double-tap reseeds the pitches. The widening is the piece. Nothing else happens, and it is enough.

title: Outside the Dream
note: Outside the Dream Syndicate, 1972/73, Conrad with Faust: violin drones over a relentless pulse, the music nothing but interference. Four sine oscillators sit near 110 Hz, offset by fractions of a hertz, and their beats are drawn as concentric arcs at the center of a dark field: each ring breathes at one pair's beat rate, brightening as the waves reinforce, thinning as they cancel. The arcs are not a visualizer; they are computed from the same phase state that drives the oscillators, a measurement of the sound's grain. Tap to start the audio (it never autoplays) and switch on Faust's two-hertz pulse, ticked by the brass marker on the bar below. Drag sideways to detune: the beats accelerate, the rings churn, and on release everything settles back toward unison, the slow swell returning. Minimal, hypnotic, and honest: the picture is the interference, and the interference is the piece.

title: Loose Connection
note: Conrad's 1973 rig: a camera on baby-carriage wheels, rolling backward and forward while rotating, catching only a few frames at intervals. The street here is procedural and endless, flat storefronts with awnings and typographic signs, MUSIC, BOOKS, DELI, and the camera never stops its two motions at once: dollying along the street while the whole world slowly rolls. But you do not see the motion; you see the record: the display takes a frame roughly every third of a second and holds it, so the smooth journey arrives as a stutter of stills, the film catching every Nth moment of a trip that never pauses. Drag to take the wheel yourself, sideways for speed, up and down for roll; release and his programmed score resumes. Double-tap reseeds the street. The looseness is the connection: between the moving world and the frames that fail to keep up.

title: Four Square
note: Four Square, 1971: four projectors, four flicker films, one room. Four panels in a grid, each running its own black-and-white block map at its own rate, four drone strings in light. Left alone they beat against each other, alignments flashing and dissolving; every ninety seconds a conductor gathers them, rates and phases easing together until all four panels strobe as a single field, holds them a breath, then lets them drift apart again. Drag across a panel to push its phase: force an alignment, or break one that is forming. Double-tap reseeds all four maps. Every panel stays under the study's frequency cap; tap the top-right corner for the reduced-motion fades. Watch for the sync. When four projectors agree, the room itself seems to blink.

title: The Yellow Movie
note: A fifty-year film, finished the day it shipped. A sheet of paper, a hand-brushed black rectangle with one drip at the corner, and inside the frame a field of white house paint. That is the whole movie. The field is yellowing: seeded from its creation date, it drifts toward cream on a fifty-year curve, and the small label at the margin states the current frame, today 0.00 of 50 years. Nothing perceptible will change while you watch, or this year, or next; a visitor in a decade will meet a slightly different frame than you did. There is no interaction, because time is the interaction and it does not take requests. Conrad called these graphic works films because they project at the speed of chemistry. Stand here a moment anyway. Somewhere in the white, 2076 is developing.

title: Straight and Narrow
note: Conrad's 1970 film with Beverly Grant: successive frames of horizontal and vertical bars, and the heady moire they produce. Full-field bar frames alternate here at a capped rate, horizontal, then vertical, with a second pattern at 1.03 times the scale interleaved so the interference fringes crawl slowly across the field. None of the fringes are drawn; your visual system manufactures them, exactly as his audiences' did, the optical twin of the beat frequencies in his drone music. Drag tunes it: sideways for rate, up and down for bar width, like focusing a tuning fork. Double-tap reseeds the pattern. Tap the top-right corner, or use reduced motion, for a slow crossfade instead of the alternation. Ten minutes, a hard stop, and it begins again. The pattern is bars. Everything else is you.

title: Twenty Hertz
note: Conrad tuned his Flicker soundtrack synth to 20 Hz, the exact point where rhythm becomes pitch. This is the soundtrack without the film: a dark room, a small pilot lamp, a meter, and one sine oscillator sweeping slowly between 4 and 40 Hz. Below the brass threshold marker at 20 Hz the lamp resolves into separate flashes and the sound is clicks, a rhythm; above it the lamp steadies and the clicks fuse into a tone. Drag sideways to sweep the oscillator with your own hand and feel the crossing happen under your finger. Tap toggles between the fixed 20 Hz and the sweep. Sound starts only when you first tap, and there is nothing else to hear: no melody, no music, one oscillator doing physics at the border of two senses.

title: The Tambura
note: Six strings, one note, fifty years: the all-E guitar of Guitar Trio, 1977, drawn as six pale lines on black. They are tuned almost, but not quite, together, and the almost is the music: interference between the micro-detuned strings shows as slow amber shimmer bands that travel along the lines, brightening where the waves agree, dimming where they quarrel. On a thirty-two-second loop the chord is struck, drifts and shimmers, settles toward near-unison as the bands slow and widen, fades, and is struck again with the next of three detune sets. There is no guitar, no hand, no pick: the lines play themselves. Chord is one; watch what it contains.

title: Footage
note: A tall panel of OSB, oriented strand board, the cheapest skin in building, carrying a photograph of itself: two procedural flake layers, the panel's actual surface and its own printed image laid on top, slightly darker, slightly off. At rest the misregistration is a whisper, eight pixels of doubt in the strands. Drag and the schism widens to thirty: every flake doubles, the depicted board sliding against the real one until the surface shimmers at two depths at once. The blue floor strip at the bottom keeps its counsel. Nothing else is depicted, because nothing else is needed: the actual and the image of the actual, failing to coincide. Slide it back to zero and feel the small relief of a thing matching itself, and how quickly the relief feels like a loss.

title: Codax
note: One painting, one color, one fictitious name: a square of saturated violet on white, signed quietly in the corner, h. codax. The color never changes. The hand does: drag and the surface scrubs between two makers, one enamel-smooth, the paint laid flat and clean as a factory finish; the other cloudy and oxidized, mottle blooming across the field, amber creeping the edges, the same violet gone weathered and doubtful. Release mid-scrub and the painting hangs between authors, half one hand, half the other. Nothing explains the device, because the device is the point: authorship as a surface treatment, identity as something a drag can revise. Leave it at the mixture you believe. The signature does not change either way.

title: The Foggy Mirror
note: Kassay's silver painting, the mirror that refuses to mirror: one tall panel of electroplated canvas on a dark ground, its surface a fog in which a room barely exists: a bright window, a dark doorway, warm and cool weather, all blurred to the edge of disappearance, the canvas weave ghosting through the metal, amber oxidation creeping the top, bottom, and left edges like the bath remembering itself. The piece has no image of its own; it only reflects, badly, on purpose. Drag and the room slides across the silver, the window traveling farther than the doorway, exactly as turning your head in front of it would do. Leave it and the reflection drifts on its own. Stand still and let the fog decide what you look like.

title: Manifestation Five
note: December 1967, rebuilt as an engine: BMPT's motif-swap, one square canvas, one ring, three authors. For twenty seconds the ring is Toroni's: a circumference of cobalt brush imprints, jittering dabs where the outline should be. Hard cut: twenty seconds of Buren, the ring become an annulus of white and vermilion stripes at the 8.7 module. Hard cut: twenty seconds of Mosset himself, the flat black outline, administrative and calm. A tiny counter keeps the takes, 01/03, 02/03, 03/03, and the loop begins again. The motif never changes; the authorship rotates under it. Watch all three and decide which hand the ring belongs to. The group's whole argument was that the question is empty.

title: The Fold
note: Mosset's single allowance of illusion: a full field of even red and white horizontal stripes, and in the lower-right corner, a painted fold. At rest the corner lies flat, betrayed only by a hairline seam and a whisper of shadow. Drag, pulling toward the upper left, and the corner peels: the flat stripes turn a corner and become a striped box, the bands continuing unbroken across the fold edge onto the flap and the revealed underside, same pigment, new angles, with a soft shadow gathering underneath. It is not a real fold and never pretends otherwise for long: it is flat paint performing depth. Peel it slowly. The stripe continuity across the hinge is the whole trick, and it never breaks.

title: TBT
note: The chameleon diamond: a square canvas hung at forty-five degrees on a dark ground, painted in TBT chameleon pigment, whose color is not a property of the canvas but of where you stand. From one side it reads teal; shift, and it warms through copper; shift again, violet, the readings even spreading across the surface at once, teal lingering at one vertex while the other warms. Your movement is the pigment: drag horizontally and walk around it without moving, the hue easing after your hand like a material remembering. Leave it alone and it slowly cycles the viewpoints on its own, thirty seconds a tour. No rainbow, no effect: one coat of paint, three honest readings. Find the angle where it cannot decide.

title: Diamond Presentation
note: The same ring canvas, one variable changed: the hang. The square hangs as a diamond, meeting the wall at a point instead of a side, its soft shadow pooling along the lower edges, and the painting itself is entirely unchanged. That is the experiment, and you run it: drag, and the canvas rotates continuously between square and diamond, any angle between, the ring riding rigidly inside its frame; let go, and it settles with a slow, weighty ease to the nearest honest orientation. Nothing else in the room moves. Presentation is the only content Mosset allows here, so present carefully. Turn it to the angle you would defend, and notice that the ring does not care.

title: The Ring
note: The canonical Mosset, drawn by a filing cabinet: a square white canvas, enamel-flat, and on it one black ring, an outline only, its stroke exactly 3.3 percent of the canvas, centered with a near-imperceptible drift. No brush texture, no expression: the hand is administrative. On a thirty-second loop the ring draws itself once, clockwise, thin to full; holds while a slow sheen crosses the enamel; then fades, and the filing starts again, each cycle's center and radius jittered by a hair, the way two hundred supposedly identical rings never quite are. Nothing to operate. Watch it be drawn. The most reproduced nothing in Swiss painting, reproduced once more, correctly.

title: The Ocean Answer
note: Why repeat the same grid for sixty years? Toroni's answer: you can look at the ocean every day, but it is never the same sea. Here is the proof, take by take: the identical cobalt lattice on warm white, twelve times in a forty-eight-second loop, four seconds a take, hard cuts between them like pages turning. The layout never moves a hair. The hand is never twice the same: pressure, rotation, paint load wander take by take, and a tiny counter in the corner, 01/12, 02/12, keeps the count so you can hunt the differences honestly. Fix your eye on one dab and ride all twelve takes. It is the same mark. It is never the same mark. That is the whole philosophy, demonstrated.

title: Column Study
note: The final support: three tall canvases stand floor to ceiling, the format of Toroni's 2025 Locarno retrospective, and down each one the imprints descend in a sparse vertical rhythm, green down the outer two, orange-red down the center. The viewpoint itself becomes the slow event: on a thirty-six-second loop the view drifts down the columns and back, the dabs passing like a meter stick being read, soft bands at top and bottom hinting that the canvases run on beyond the frame. Nothing else happens, and the monumentality is exactly that restraint: three columns of the same gesture, repeated at the scale of architecture. Stand in front of them. Let the drift carry your eye down and return it. The column is the last wall the brush ever needed.

title: Toile Cirée
note: The imprints on waxed fabric, Toroni's strangest support: a near-black ground with the oily sheen of toile ciree, and across it a dense brick-offset grid of ochre dabs, each with its bristle streaks and a thin gloss line where the brush landed. At one corner the fabric's folded hem turns under, a small triangle of material reality. The system itself never changes; what moves is the material: on a thirty-second loop a slow sheen wave crosses the field diagonally every twelve seconds, the oiliness traveling like light over a tablecloth, the dabs holding their intervals through it. Painted, never photographic. Run your eyes along a row and watch the sheen pass under the marks. The fabric breathes; the method does not.

title: Window Glass
note: Toroni on the street: a grid of dark glass panes in pale aluminum mullions at night, and on the center pane, painted directly on the glass as he did at the Swiss Institute, three white imprints that never move. Behind the glass the gallery glows faintly and breathes on a forty-second cycle, dim to bright and back, while reflection streaks slide slowly across the panes. That is all the motion there is, and it belongs to the light, not the marks: the imprints stay exactly where the brush left them while the city and the room take turns showing through. Stand outside and watch the window breathe. The support is the environment; the painting is three dabs of white holding still inside it.

title: The Red Doorway
note: The system-to-explore piece of the Toroni set: a white wall over a parquet floor, vermilion imprints climbing it in the regular brick-offset rhythm, and a doorway in the left third that the grid refuses to ignore: the rows bend around its frame, dabs bunching along the edges, none inside the opening. Two small canvases on the right carry black and orange imprints of their own. Now the experiment: drag the doorway sideways. It slides, and the entire field re-wraps around its new position instantly and mechanically, no bounce, no theatrics, the grid recomputing itself around the architecture in real time. Release it anywhere; the wall accepts the new arrangement as if it had always been so. The grid is the constant. You are the variable.

title: Sail Race
note: A regatta of pure stripe: three tall triangular sails, white canvas banded red, green, and blue, crossing a flat warm-gray sea on parallel diagonal lanes, a horizon line low in the frame and nothing else, no hulls, no water, no wake but a faint echo of stripes trailing at fifteen percent. Their speeds stand in exact integer ratios over a forty-eight-second loop, so the blue laps the green, the green laps the red, overtakes happen mid-frame, and at the loop's close every sail is precisely where it began, ready to race again. Each sail billows on its own phase, canvas breathing. Wind, not motors. Pick a sail and follow it through an overtake; the crossing is the race, and the race never ends.

title: In Situ
note: The strictest recipe in the set: the frame itself is the site, and everything in the picture is measured off it. A vertical band of white and deep-blue stripes stands exactly one module in from the left edge and runs the full height; a second hugs the top-right corner like a blocked doorway; a third follows the frame's own diagonal, corner to corner. Nothing else exists. A small threshold block breathes at the bottom-right, but only when the frame is wider than tall: rotate to portrait and it simply is not there, a condition of the site, not a decoration. Resize the window and the bands slide to their new anchors, re-measuring themselves in a third of a second: the visual tool, laid down fresh each time. Placed, never composed.

title: Encasement
note: One of the 1967-69 Encasements: a vacuum-formed panel in a coved white room, its corners rounded away so the architecture never quite resolves. The panel itself is almost nothing, a slightly different white, but inside its edges runs a thin line of neon-bright blue-white, and from that line the glow bleeds outward in a soft halo until the panel seems to be dissolving into the wall that holds it. Drag and the light's fall shifts with your viewpoint, a small parallax in the halo. Tap and the panel changes temperature: white to blue to rose to white, crossfading slowly, the edge line re-tuning itself. The panel never moves. Only the light changes its mind. Stand in the cove and watch it fail to be an object.

title: Electric Light
note: From the lightboxes of 1968, when she powered argon with a Tesla coil in the studio: a white slab hangs in a dark room on monofilament threads too thin to see, glowing with a spectral, sourceless light, brightest at its center, graying at the edges, its halo bleeding softly onto the wall behind. There is no lamp and no switch; the light simply is. It breathes on a slow forty-five-second cycle, and underneath the breath a faint mains flicker worries it, fast, tiny, irregular, the way real current behaves. Drag up or down to dim or brighten it yourself. The room stays dark. Sit with it the way you would sit with an aquarium: nothing happens, beautifully.

title: White Light Field
note: Seven vertical bands of white and warm gray, full-bleed, and at first glance almost nothing: until the light moves. Each band is full of glass microspheres and gestural horizontal brushwork, but both stay invisible until the band's angle to the light is exactly right; then the band ignites from inside, warming toward gold, the beads and strokes suddenly legible, while its neighbors stay flat and quiet. The light sweeps slowly, thirty seconds across, so the bands flare one after another like a row of windows catching the sun in sequence. Drag to aim the light yourself and hold a band at its brightest. Monochrome plus light: the color was never applied, it is retrieved. Stand still and let the sweep come to you.

title: Excursus Square
note: Homage to the Square, cubed: four nested squares and nothing else, no outlines, no shadows, the bands separated only by the chromatic edge itself. But the bands are instruments, not colors on a chart: over a six-minute drift each band's hue wanders a few degrees on its own slow cycle, the value ladder held steady, so the relationships keep reorganizing: the rust band advances, then recedes; the deep slate center sinks, then floats. An Albers study rebuilt as a time piece, after his Excursus at Dia. Double-tap and the whole stack reseeds to a new family of muted ochres, rusts, creams and slates, crossfading over four seconds. Nothing rotates, nothing scales: only color moves. Watch one band until it changes its mind about its neighbors.

title: Dot Field
note: The dot paintings: from across the room, a blank off-white canvas, nothing on it at all. Lean in, and it is covered in minute green and red dots, hundreds of them, each placed by hand, denser toward the middle, and once your eye finds them they will not sit still: they dance and lift off the surface, the hide-and-seek color play he built in 1964. Scroll or pinch to lean in here: the dots emerge and start their dance, then subside back under the threshold when you let go. Drag through the field and a wake of dancing follows your finger, settling over about ten seconds. Double-tap and the canvas blanks, then a new arrangement of dots settles in. From a distance: nothing. Up close: everything.

title: Alpha Tunnel
note: Roden Crater's Alpha Tunnel as an instrument you look through: a long stone corridor in one-point perspective, course rings shrinking toward the Image Stone at the vanishing point, a pale shaft of light falling from the tunnel mouth, dust drifting in it. The stone is a camera obscura, and what it shows is computed from the real date, nothing else: in the southernmost-sunset window, December 11 to 31, the sun's image burns on the stone at the position the declination dictates; near a major lunar standstill it holds a dim moon; the rest of the year, like today, it shows near-darkness and a faint outline, exactly as the real tunnel would. No label names the date or the event. The piece is the instrument. Watch the dust; come back in December.

title: September Blues
note: Trying to Remember the Color of the Sky on That September Morning: a full-bleed grid of hand-painted watercolor squares on warm paper, nearly a thousand tiles, every one a slightly different blue and nothing else, ever. Each tile is laid in overlapping brush strokes with wobbling edges and uneven fill, so the hand shows in every square. Once a minute a slow wet wave crosses the field: tiles near the front briefly deepen and saturate, as if freshly painted, then dry back. Tap a tile and it holds wet for five seconds. The grid never reseeds and never decorates itself; it stays fixed and quiet, like his. Watch the wave pass.

title: Alignment
note: A grid of cells on black, each holding four quarter-circle arcs in saturated colors, each cell rotating on its own phase, so the field looks like scattered rainbow shrapnel. Then a wave of phase passes diagonally through the grid and cell after cell snaps into complete circles, a brief moment of total order, before the rotations drift apart again. Two alignment waves cross the loop, and the circles are never drawn directly: they only emerge when the arcs agree. Twenty-four seconds, seamless. Watch for the moment of order. Tap to reseed the phases.

title: Detach
note: One amorphous black mass on white, built from thousands of tiny square pixels, and the pixels keep leaving. Edge pixels detach, drift outward, pause, and fly home; the mass slowly breathes between near-circle and oval. Around it float loose colored squares, pink, yellow, teal, violet, that are sometimes drawn toward the mass and sometimes repelled, their mood flipping on a slow timer. Now and then a small white plus flashes inside the mass and a thin black square frame blinks around it. Every mark is an axis-aligned square; there are no circles anywhere. Drag through the mass and you knock pixels loose and push the loose squares; they settle and re-attach after. Tap to reseed.

title: Noise Halftone
note: A strict grid of circles on white, built exactly in his live order: grid first, shape second, one binary rule third, noise fourth. Each circle's radius is set by a slow noise field, so the grid breathes like a halftone: swells of big circles, shallows of fine dots, traveling diagonally across the field. The one rule: circles left of a slow-swaying vertical divide are solid black, circles right of it are hollow rings, and the divide sits near fifty-five percent of the width. Black and white only, circles and rings only. Thirty seconds and the loop closes exactly where it began. Watch it breathe. Tap to reseed the field.

title: Unknown Script
note: An 8 by 8 grid of sixty-four invented glyphs on black, each assembled from the same two part types only: rounded-rectangle strokes, like the bones of a seven-segment display, and dots at the nodes. Every cell holds a different sign, yet the whole field reads as one coherent unknown alphabet. Slowly the script rewrites itself: a wave travels the grid and each visited cell swaps a single stroke or dot, never a whole glyph at once, so the language appears to evolve under your eyes. No letter, no digit, nothing you can read: the meaning stays locked. Watch it rewrite. Tap to reseed a fresh set of sixty-four.

title: Hot Spot
note: A steel globe floating in blackness, human-height, barely visible as a dark body with a faint latitude and longitude frame, its continents traced in glowing red wire: the whole planet as a danger zone. The globe turns almost too slowly to notice, one full turn in ninety seconds, the wire ending cleanly at the limb, a ghost of the far hemisphere showing through the steel. It opens on the Atlantic: Africa centered, the Americas at the edges. Drag sideways to spin it yourself; on release it eases back to its slow drift. Tap and a spark pulse travels along one continent wire and fades. No borders, no labels: continents only.

title: Plegaria Muda
note: Silent prayer: the stacked tables of the burial field, seen edge-on as dark horizontal slabs, surface to surface, with bands of dark soil between them. Through the soil, thousands of thin sage-green grass blades grow, sway, die back, and regrow, each on its own slow cycle of growing, holding, and fading, denser toward the middle rows, sparser at the edges. Nothing here is loud: the green is desaturated, the motion is weather. A burial field that tends itself. Move through it and the blades bend aside and spring back, as if you were walking the rows. Tap to reseed the field.

title: Chimba Hue
note: Two banks, two musics, one river. The frame is a vertical triptych: on the left, La Chimba, warm, dense and rhythmic, a field of small bright tick-stars pulsing in interlocking patterns on a two-three-four weave of periods; on the right, cooler and sparser, long slow arcs drifting and breathing; between them the river band, its particles drifting both ways and net down, flecked with foam. The banks are deliberately not symmetrical: they face each other like two choirs singing different music. Drag horizontally across the river and ripples cross the band; when they reach a bank, that bank answers, the left re-phasing its rhythm, the right swelling once. Call and response, with water as the mediator.

title: Combarbalita Choir
note: Lithophony: nine monolithic blocks of combarbalita, the Chilean stone carved with complex internal tubes, standing in a dark field like a megalithic circle. Each rounded slab, pink or mauve, carries its own carved channel system on its face, winding walls and separations, no two alike, glyphs rather than texture. Stone is still: nothing moves until you strike. Tap a block and a luminous ring radiates from the strike point across its face, fading with mineral slowness, while a low resonance sounds, pitched by the block. Tap the same block twice quickly for a harder strike, deeper ring, longer decay. Drag across the row to play them as a sweep. Then silence and stillness again, which is also the instrument.

title: Santamaska
note: His 1997 engraving as a living mask. One frontal face, strictly symmetric by construction, its geometry and expression fixed forever; only the line grammar changes. At one pole, Nasca simplicidad extraordinaria: the face in about a dozen bold strokes, one of them cinnabar. At the other, Santamaria locura de las figuras: the same face filled with over a hundred fine interlaced filaments and hooks in charcoal, every stroke splitting and multiplying as the grammar parameter drifts across a forty-second loop, dwelling near each pole. The symmetry never breaks, verified to within antialiasing. Watch-only; it is a mask, beheld.

title: Cien Pesos
note: The coin story: in 1999 a man from the Casa de Moneda asked permission to use his drawing as the model for the hundred-peso coin, and perhaps millions of reproductions have been made. A woman's portrait is generated entirely from engraved contour lines in silver on near-black, nested offset curves tightening on the nose and lips, loosening through the hair, inside a thin copper rim. The medallion turns slowly on its own; drag horizontally to spin it with inertia, edge-on it compresses to a sliver, and every full rotation stamps one faint copy that drifts backward and fades, at most twelve, the reproductions accumulating behind the original. No coin imagery, no symbols: only linework that earns its place.

title: Humo Adentro
note: His doctrine in code: el viaje humo adentro, the inner smoke journey. Four hundred smoke particles curl and drift across the paper on a slow ambient loop, and inside the smoke a face is built fresh from parameters at every reseed: brow, eyes, nose and lips drawn as directional pencil hatch whose visibility breathes with the smoke itself, fading where the field thickens, sharpening where it thins, never fully arriving. The eyes look out at you and their pupils follow your pointer, a face watching from that world toward this one. One small ember point glows low-left. Drag to tear the smoke; the face strains and reforms as the field settles. Double-tap for a new face.

title: Profecía
note: The Condor and Eagle prophecy: two forms of intelligence that split, broke the balance of the world, and are reuniting now. From the top-left a silver eagle, sharp and geometric, spirals inward trailing gold dust; from the bottom-right a condor, a massive indigo stain with pale feathers, spirals in to meet it. At the exact center they merge into a single new form, genuinely neither bird: a cinnabar creature with V-raised wings and a round body that hangs for a held moment and pulses once, before the loop unwinds and the two separate again along their spirals, leaving only their fading trails in an empty sky. Watch-only, forty seconds. No flags, no symbols; the merge is the whole piece.

title: La Transición
note: Her Rodin thesis as a picture that refuses to settle: el movimiento es la transicion de una actitud a otra. One horse, built from a single procedural kit, exists only in-between: seven translucent silhouettes interpolated between a gathered attitude and an extended one, ochre ghosts behind, sienna ahead, the middle frame solid iron black, gold dust breathing in its mane. The interpolation sweeps back and forth over twenty-four seconds but is clamped so it never reaches either keyframe: no canonical gallop, no resolved horse, ever, just the frozen transition breathing on pale paper. No blur, no speed lines. Watch-only.

title: Una Tarde de Verano
note: His garden-scale vignettes as sketchbook pages: one small scene per page inside a wobbly hand-drawn border on a vast dark ground. A mouse beside a tulip, twitching its nose; a cicada clinging to a twig, shell trembling; an owl at sunset before a pale moon, blinking slowly. The subject never fills the page; negative space is the point. Drag sideways to turn the page, both directions. Double-tap and a new vignette in the same grammar joins the book: a chick, a fox kit, a beetle.

title: All'alba
note: His own wordless book as a fixed-scene loop: one night landscape that never changes its layout, a branch, a silk cocoon hanging center-frame, five flowers lower right, stars above. Over about seventy-five seconds night becomes day: the sky gradient climbs through violet and rose to a low gold band (no sun disc), the flowers bloom petal by petal, each petal unrolling from its curl, the cocoon opens and a moth emerges, flaps twice and settles, three birds cross once, then dusk re-curls everything and night returns. Tap to call one dawn immediately.

title: El Bosque Infinito
note: His FANTASTIC FOREST concertina as an infinite strip: three depth layers of hand-wobbled trees (near trunks large and dark, far trunks thin and blue-gray, no two canopies alike) scroll past under a slow day-and-night drift. Drag sideways to unfold the concertina; the layers parallax and the strip never ends, wrapping seamlessly. Hidden in the canopy, one small creature per stretch, an owl by its amber eyes, a mouse, a fox, a hummingbird, never announced, only discoverable. Double-tap and the forest regrows from new seeds.

title: The Mirror Is the Law
note: Her symmetrical floral tree: a tree rises from a sunflower base, branches, leaves and pink blossoms in strict vertical mirror symmetry. Every so often the tree tries a small asymmetric flourish, and over the next seconds the mirror gently corrects it, fading a twin in on the other side until symmetry is restored. Drag for a gust and a few buds sprout off-law; tap to plant one deliberate asymmetric flower. Both get absorbed. Symmetry always wins in the end.

title: White on White
note: Her paper in a scale of whites: one continuous white sheet, embossed dunes flowing diagonally, incised line rivers, and exactly three sharp cut slits revealing warm shadow beneath. There is no color and no input at all; the light breathes on a sixty-second cycle and the reliefs appear and dissolve. This one is only for looking.

title: Strip Book
note: Her harlequinade as an object: five horizontal paper strips stack into one day garden (sun, ferns, hanging pods, the elephant pair, a creature band, a green hill), seams and curl shadows visible, a thin spine at left. Tap a strip and it flicks over, flat and stepped, to its slice of the night garden: navy, perforated stars, the elephants asleep. Flip all five for the whole night; tap any strip to flip it back.

title: The Smudge
note: A macro of her embossing: beige fibrous paper at extreme close-up, a field of small raised organic reliefs thinning toward the edges, and at the heart one faint red smudge. Raking light orbits once in forty seconds; the reliefs surface and sink as it passes. Double-tap to reseed the field; the smudge never moves, it is the anchor. Almost still, on purpose.

title: Un Jardín
note: Her 2020 creature world alive: a layered papercut garden (ferns, perforated pods, curling stems) with the black elephant and pale-blue companion anchored center-left and small Hugos blob creatures wandering the low layers. All motion is stepped stopmotion, no smooth tweening anywhere, her native grammar. Tap the paper and a new creature is cut and wanders in (up to twelve); drag to rustle the nearest layer.

title: Walk Into the Garden
note: Her tunnel book as a dolly shot: six nested cut-paper frames recede into the Los Hugos garden (ferns, perforated seed pods, a leafy arch), and deep inside, small, the black elephant and its pale-blue companion under a perforated moon. Drag up to walk in; the frames separate with true parallax and the walk ends at the moon. Tap a frame and it lifts toward you for a beat.

title: Cosas de Todos los Días
note: Her register as a still life in motion (her bio line is the title: dibujos y cosas de todos los dias): six objects from her strips on a kitchen table, los vasos de Noah, las plumas de Emi, las semillas en el frasco, el crayon buscado, la hoja, la piedra, each carrying exactly one touch of her soft blue. They drift very slowly and resettle into a new constellation every twenty seconds. Nothing happens, tenderly. Tap one for its name.

Her kid-logic strip, verbatim: Noah, llevá las cosas de a una. Si, lo que pasa es que tengo dos manos. 1+1=2. ¡Pua! Four notebook panels; panel 1 is inked and the rest wait in pencil. Each tap inks the next panel at reading pace; there is no autoplay. The mother is the butt of the joke, never the child. Blue appears only on Noah's shirt, and only once his panels ink in.

title: ¿Dónde Estar?
note: The migrant's doubt as a pendulum: Lisbon (red tram, tiled facades) on the left, Buenos Aires (cafe, wide avenue) on the right, and her small avatar with the red suitcase on a tightrope between them, the empty between-space the largest thing on the page. Drag her toward a city and it brightens while the other fades; let go and she swings back to the middle. There is no arrival state. Tap a city for her words.

title: Río y Llanto
note: Her jewel, the contradiction: one figure laughing with X-eyes while crying, a jajaja bubble on one side, a red wound on the other, a rubber duck at her feet. Drag up and humor leads, drag down and pain leads, but the opposite never disappears (the mix is clamped so neither register ever drops to zero), and tap makes her laugh and cry at full force for one beat.

title: Quero a Minha Mãe
note: Her repeated-figure sequencer from the Gravidez cover: eight white bodies on flat loud red, the same body redrawn eight times with the belly growing, while the bubble overhead decays (QUERO A MINHA MAE... MAE... M... ...MAE?) and comes back shouting. The first holds a pregnancy test and a SIM sign. Drag sideways to scrub the sequence; tap a figure to freeze her mid-stutter.

title: Festejan las Gallinas
note: Direct from her 2026 embroidery: the three chickens celebrate on dusty-rose cloth, magenta in the center, turquoise stars stitched above, pecking in turn at the scattered seed-stitches in a seamless loop. The colophon along the bottom carries the real date of the day you open it, Rosario. Tap the colophon to re-stitch it; drag for parallax.

title: Más Íntimo Que la Ropa Interior
note: Her claim as a piece: looking through someone's library is more intimate than their underwear drawer. A tall shelf in color bands (reds, blues, yellows, greens, neutrals), and every one of the eighty-odd spines is a tiny invented book cover, generated, none repeated, no real titles. Drag a book out to see its cover; tap to hold it out; tap again to reshelve.

title: Manet Duerme la Siesta
note: A tiny moment, watch-only: Manet asleep on a green sofa in a big quiet room, his finished canvas leaning against the wall beside him, night at the window, a lamp glowing, a cat asleep on the rug. His chest breathes slowly; the cat's tail flicks once per loop; nobody wakes him. Drag for a slight parallax.

title: Se Cayó Colgando el Matisse
note: A museum calamity on a loop: a tiny forged Matisse (an homage, not a copy) hangs center wall while a small worker on a wobbling ladder tries to straighten it. Once per loop he falls, the picture tilts, the two tiny onlookers flinch, and a guard calmly walks in and re-hangs everything. Deadpan throughout. Drag the ladder to wobble it harder.

title: El Río
note: One eternal blue hour on a wide river, watch-only: a woman submerged to the shoulders, a crocodile, a snake, a bat hanging upside down holding a pink heart, a fox wading by distant polite flames, and a crescent moon with a red droplet. Everything weeps; nothing is explained. Tears fall in one seamless loop and the bat sways. Drag to pan across the panorama.

title: Soy Otra
note: Her rule as a piece: CADA VEZ QUE ME DIBUJO SOY OTRA. A seated self-portrait in strict black and white that redraws itself stroke by stroke every time you tap: new hair, new tattoos, a septum ring, a flower earring, a different gaze, never the same face twice in a row. Drag on the hair and it grows.

title: Es Aquí
note: Satanás keeps a reserved seat for people who call you crazy for no reason: a jolly red devil presents a black spiked chair oozing red, beside a cobra and a skull, in flat flickering flames. Tap the chair, the snake, or the skull.

title: Nine Small Dooms
note: A giant black cat with yellow slit eyes presides over seven vignette circles: a parrot and a ghost, a palm tree, a crouched smoker, a duck with flame eyes, a smiley kebab, a smoking door, a closed door. Watch them drift.

title: Silent Nine
note: Nine deadpan panels of tiny office rituals, the speech balloons holding only punctuation: ..., ?, !, ... Tap to generate a new silent story.

title: Forest Census
note: A field-guide plate of twelve distinct mushrooms, every fourth one drawn as a hatched ink study with a Latin label. Watch the spores drift.

title: The Bewitched Witch
note: A kind witch sits side-saddle on a giant spotted mushroom, her bird, rabbit, hedgehog and fox around her, a glowing pumpkin house below and a strip of six mushrooms underneath. Watch the fireflies drift.

title: Hortus
note: A walled garden of giant frogs around a red tree, and a woman whose pet frog keeps flicking its tongue at her nose. Drag to scatter the frogs.

title: Two Riders
note: Twin archways in a pink marble frame: a rider on a yellow horse under a pink sun, a rider on a pink horse under a crescent moon. Watch the sun sink as the moon rises.

title: Saints and Suns
note: A quilt of gold-edged diamonds, a haloed saint on checkerboard in each, blue suns in the gaps. Tap to reshuffle the quilt.

title: Two Heads, One Flower
note: Two mirrored heads crowned with flame-flowers, lips almost touching. Drag to lean them toward each other.

title: Night Panther
note: A mirrored roaring panther poster on flat red: yellow ring eyes, blue muzzle, white fangs and whiskers. Watch it breathe.

title: Città Blocks
note: A fauvist block city crossed by rainbow ribbons, one tiny black figure walking a ledge. Watch the layers drift.

title: Balloon Belly
note: A tiny mother holds a balloon the size of a belly while a giant orange face grins in from the other half of the frame. Drag the balloon.

title: Giant on a Minipony
note: A giant-headed woman in a striped dress riding a pony a quarter her size, inside a blue painted frame. Watch them amble.

title: Island of Small Things
note: A giant black island stuffed with tiny bottles, cups and stars, three cream creatures riding its top, under a hand-lettered invented phrase. Watch the motifs drift.

title: Minotauro
note: A huge black minotaur in three riso inks, wearing hot-pink boots and clutching a white envelope purse. Watch it breathe and snort.

title: Bear Page
note: A giant blue bear whose belly is a newspaper page, waving one white paw. Watch it breathe.

title: Letter Sprinkle
note: Pink cliffs, striped birch trunks, teal water, and tiny letters sprinkled only inside the foliage and the waves. Watch the water drift.

title: Palm Tones
note: Flat palm glyphs and star dots on near-black, one of five printed colorways. Watch them sway; tap to change colorway.

title: Exploded Serif
note: A giant serif capital pulled apart along its axes like a technical diagram. Drag the fragments; double-tap for a new letter.

title: Literal Idiom
note: An amphora wearing the idiom literally: footprints stride around its belly under the words CON I PIEDI. Tap for a new pairing.

title: Selva
note: A burnt-orange Dante profile in laurel, ringed by sage foliage and halftone dots inside a zigzag border. Tap for a new profile.

title: The Embrace
note: Two figures embrace under foliage while hat figures sway and a crescent moon glows. Watch them breathe.

title: Blue Garden
note: An underwater garden in arched niches: orange-red corals, vases and striped fish on deep blue. Watch the fish drift.

title: Panel Wall
note: A mural facade of framed panels: figures, coral glyphs, lettering marks and patterns in mustard, teal and rust. Watch the motifs crossfade.

title: The Capsule
note: A woman sits curled inside a giant red-and-white capsule. Drag to tilt it; she slides gently to the low end.

title: Roofwalker
note: A woman stands barefoot on the roof of a doll-scale house under an enormous sky. Watch the clouds drift.

title: The Path
note: A two-panel pilgrimage: a lone walker follows a winding path to a distant white church. Drag to move the walker. Tap to reseed the route.

title: Pink Manager
note: A one-panel portrait generator in magenta-skin grammar, tonal first, colorway second. Tap to reseed the pose and colorway. Drag to nudge the head.

title: Door Policy
note: One glowing doorway in a dark surround, a warm office inside. Drag the door. Tap to reseed the office.

title: Headcount
note: A suited manager sprouts his own stretched heads like petals. Drag to sprout more. Double-tap to reseed.

title: Quoted
note: His eyes are quotation marks, and every blink swaps the punctuation. Drag the quotes. Tap for a new pair.

title: Mucha Siren
note: An art-nouveau siren whose ribbon hair never stops moving. Tap for a new title word and gown.

title: Belleville Metro
note: A metro station grown into a garden of books, baskets and hanging plants. Tap for a new station.

title: The Big Disc
note: One huge flat disc hangs over a quiet city edge, breathing through three skies. Watch the disc breathe.

title: Word Shadow
note: A glossy lemon stands before a wall made of its own name. Drag to slide the word; double-tap for a new word and subject.

title: Abstract Fruits
note: After Angelina Bambina's abstract fruits: four seamless fruit patterns in a grid - leaves on mustard, pomegranates in teal and pink, pomegranates on soft pink, speckled dots on gray - each tile breathing gently while its colours rotate through the harvest schemes. Tap to re-seed the patterns. Tap to re-seed.

title: Five Women, One Pink Ground
note: After Angelina Bambina's five women: five busts in a half-ring on a flowered pink ground, every woman in her own pattern, swaying on her own rhythm while a beaded necklace swings. Tap to bring the next woman forward. Tap to rotate the ring.

title: Self-Care Waltz
note: After Yael Hofri's self-care waltz: a woman dancing barefoot at night in pink headphones, wine glass raised, music notes rising, two cats asleep on the rug in the lamplight. Watch only. Watch only.

title: Mood Boosters
note: After Kitty O'Rourke's Mood Boosters for May: four little calendar joys, a sunglassed sun over brighter days are coming, pockets full of flowers, a beach day with a dripping ice cream, and a polka-dot umbrella twirling through April showers. Watch only. Watch only.

title: Fruit Fashion
note: After Kitty O'Rourke's fruit fashion: a woman in a watermelon bucket hat holding a pear stamped FRESH, then an afro and lemon-print dress, then banana earrings and a toucan balanced on a fruit stack. Tap and the next look slides in. Tap for the next character.

title: DOGUE
note: After Kitty O'Rourke's DOGUE: a brown poodle cover girl in a red beret, sunglasses and a heart-print jacket on hot pink, masthead across the top and cover lines down the side. Tap and the lines re-set from her humour pool, best girl, wag more, treat yourself. Tap for new cover lines.

title: Funk My Life
note: After Kitty O'Rourke's funk poster: a woman with a huge afro and flower earrings, chin up inside a pink gig-poster frame on dark plum, FUNK MY LIFE arching over her in hand-lettered caps that groove slowly while her earrings swing and the stars twinkle. Watch only. Watch only.

title: Scooter Girl
note: After Kitty O'Rourke's first scooter girl: a woman pushing off on a kick-scooter over mustard, daisy tee, purple patterned pants, a net bag spilling flowers, her spotted dachshund trotting at the front wheel. Drag and the whole scene rolls. Drag to roll.

title: Noodle Lift
note: After Yeti Iglesias's first ramen: a red bowl of orange broth on hot pink, egg, narutomaki spirals and nori, a neon-yellow hand lifting ten noodle strands on dark chopsticks that sway and steam. Tap the bowl and the chopsticks lift higher. Tap the bowl.

title: Neon Shoe
note: After Yeti Iglesias's Vans maximalism: a giant white sneaker on a checkerboard floor under a hot pink sky, neon leaves, five watching eyes on stems, a watermelon slice, a huge pencil, and a black cat in headphones on the toe, phone flickering. Drag and the diorama pans. Drag to pan.

title: Pattern Walker
note: After Yeti Iglesias's pattern-stacked walker: a girl mid-stride on peachy cream in an orange polka-dot top and olive pants with pink stripes, a scalloped tote with a cat face bouncing at her shoulder, a pink mushroom book in her hands, autumn leaves falling around her. Watch only. Watch only.

title: Sax Bouquet
note: After Yeti Iglesias's metamorphosis: a girl in a red polka-dot dress playing saxophone on flat pink, her waist melting into stems while the bell bursts into a bouquet of cat heads, two-tone flowers and leaves that slowly blooms and relaxes as note-petals drift up. Watch only. Watch only.

title: Eat Your Colors
note: After Yeti Iglesias's Eat Your Colors: six giant vegetables on flat orange, each split into two clashing tones, eggplant, carrot, garlic, pepper, zucchini and celery, breathing slowly while one at a time does a small wiggle under twinkling sparkles. Watch only. Watch only.

title: Tuesday Funtivity
note: After Yeti Iglesias's Tuesday Funtivity: her orange cat with sparkle eyes and a green dotted scarf, sitting in a gold-latticed leaf bag beside a big pumpkin on hot pink, autumn leaves falling through starbursts. Drag and a gust streams through the leaves. Drag to gust.

title: Coffee Cats
note: After Yeti Iglesias's black coffee cats: a giant two-tone cup on cream, four black cats with yellow eyes emerging from the coffee while purple steam curls and orbs drift. Tap the cup and they dip with a splash, ripple the coffee and bob back up. Tap the cup.

title: Cat Window
note: After Yeti Iglesias's Golden Sun: an arched window on deep olive, a huge stippled orange sun in the arch, and on the checkered sill an orange striped cat flicking its tail beside a green planter and a red polka-dot mug breathing steam. Watch only. Watch only.

title: Sleeve
note: After Nina Clausonet's packaging: a tall navy sleeve tossed with coral tulips, cream stars, wheat and little women, its title band in flat geometric letters, a few motifs escaped into the cream margin and drifting up like seeds. Drag to turn the sleeve, double-tap for a new scatter. Drag to rotate, double-tap to re-scatter.

title: Bear Hug
note: After Nina Clausonet's 2020 seed: her muse hugging a huge cream polar bear on blush, both in red, her paper crown tilted, a brown tree behind them, as they rock gently together in the falling snow and the bear's ear twitches once a turn. Watch only. Watch only.

title: Pink Water
note: After Nina Clausonet's Monet homage: her muse standing in pink water, flat pink and purple lily pads on dark teal, hot-pink dress, teal umbrella high, hair and scarf streaming behind her under a pink sky. A single white petal crosses now and then. Watch only. Watch only.

title: Costume Triple
note: After Nina Clausonet's costume resolution: her muse dressed by the prompt dice, the animal worn as a print, the thing worn as a prop, opening on the jaguar turtleneck and the giant fuchsia bow. Double-tap to deal her a new costume, drag to tilt the portrait. Double-tap to deal again.

title: Shrine
note: After Nina Clausonet's body-as-landscape: her muse in profile on deep navy, her shawl a purple mountain night holding a tiny manger, palms and a winding path under an eight-point star that breathes light at her sternum. Watch only. Watch only.

title: Hair River
note: After Nina Clausonet's hair river: her white-haired muse in profile on textured gold, her hair leaving her head as a broad white river carrying three teal birds, golden leaves and white petals across the frame, a flat sunburst behind her. Watch only. Watch only.

title: Snow Cello
note: After Anna Galitskaya's winter leopard: a leopard in a snowy clearing at night, bowing a cello while the snow falls and small gold notes lift off the strings and fade. Watch only. Watch only.

title: The Fox Lady
note: After Anna Galitskaya's Fellow Fox: one fox, six professions, librarian among the book spines, baker, astronomer, gardener, cellist, ice-skater, each scene assembling around her as she walks in. Double-tap to send her off to the next job. Double-tap to change scene.

title: Mushroom Hat Parade
note: After Anna Galitskaya's costume parade: six animals marching across the dark in their one big costume piece, a kitten under a mushroom cap, an elephant in a star tutu, a frog hat, a poncho, a cello carried like a banner, neon flat on near-black. Watch only. Watch only.

title: Nine Cats
note: After Anna Galitskaya's cat contact sheet: eight cats in costume around her wordmark, a gardener in overalls, a scholar with telescope, a frog hat on a watermelon, a knitted cactus hugged close, all breathing softly in their cells. Tap a cat to recostume it. Tap a cat.

title: Triple Prompt
note: After Anna Galitskaya's Wonderful Winter Week: a prompt engine in one character, one garment, one animal, one thing per deal, a jaguar in a knitted accessory holding a festive headband and seven stranger meetings after it. Double-tap to deal the next triple, drag to sway the model. Double-tap to deal again.

title: Wimmelwald
note: After Anna Galitskaya's Wimmelwald: a snowy forest village at dusk, candle gold in the windows, a frozen lake below, and ten tiny stories hiding in it, skating bears, a badger family with a tree, gnomes at the bakery, a letter fox, a choir of mice. Tap a scene to lean in close, double-tap to step back. Tap a hidden scene.

title: The Secret Life of the Still Life
note: After Maryna Lagereva's still life doctrine: pears and a squash on a wooden table, watercolor quiet but quietly alive, the pears leaning together like conspirators, the stem curling, a beetle crossing once a minute, under her line: if your pictures do not tell a story, they are worthless. Drag near a pear and it leans to listen. Drag to lean a pear.

title: What Does This Bean Become?
note: After Maryna Lagereva's bean game: one ink bean on watercolor paper that refuses to stay a bean, an acorn dreaming of Napoleon, a rabbit swimming in borscht, an egg becoming a chick, each tap morphing it one stage further. Tap to transform it, double-tap for a fresh bean. Tap to morph.

title: Cloud Dancer Tiles
note: After Maryna Lagereva's Delft whimsy: 64 hand-wobbled tiles in strict Delft blue on white, cats, cupcakes, waves, palms, tomatoes, sailboats, books and hearts where the windmills used to be, and one Cloud Dancer tile hiding a single tiny cloud. A glaze shimmer sweeps as tiles redraw themselves. Watch only. Watch only.

title: Toile, But Make It Yoga
note: After Maryna Lagereva's toile subversion: classic Toile de Jouy vignettes on warm paper, but the scenes are yoga poses, warrior, tree, downward dog, dancer, lotus, cobra, child and crescent, inked in loud coral, teal, mustard and plum, breathing slowly like held poses. Watch only. Watch only.

title: Peaceful Birch
note: After Jen K's Peaceful Birch: eleven pale birch trunks on a moody teal-black ground, black bark marks, sage leaves low in the understory and gold leaf-dots falling slowly through a faint drifting mist. Watch only. Watch only.

title: Palm Springs Fever
note: After Jen K's Palm Springs fever dream: a flat midcentury desert, banded sunset sky, low sun, dunes and one palm silhouette, with two translucent strata sliding over it, teal cacti and stars below, big purple paisleys and sunbursts above. Watch only. Watch only.

title: Witchy Woman
note: After Jen K's Witchy Woman: a dense jewel-tone floral toss on near-black plum, poppies, daisies and chrysanthemums with gold moons, evil-eye dots and crystal shards in every gap, blooms pulsing as the gold shimmers. Drag to carry a moonlight through it. Drag to carry the moonlight.

title: Boho Jungle
note: After Jen K's Boho Jungle: five flat hero animals on light beige, a spotted leopard, striped tigers and a zebra packed in spiky leaves and berry dots with no space left over, leaves swaying as the animals breathe. Drag near an animal and it turns toward you, then settles. Drag to turn.

title: Romantsy Toile
note: After Jen K's Romantasy Toile: purple line-art vignettes on cream, dragons, castles, books, swords and crowns in half-drop, no filled shapes, a faint sparkle over them, the whole field inking itself in, holding, and fading to redraw. Watch only. Watch only.

title: Marine Building Fan
note: After Jen K's Marine Building fan: an art-deco sunburst on near-black, 36 gold ray bundles spreading 140 degrees with cream moons, eyes and crystals shrinking toward the arc and one oxblood band, a shimmer sweeping the rays as they breathe. Watch only. Watch only.

title: Poe Traits
note: After Julianne Haness's Poe-traits: portrait medallions of Poe, dark hair, moustache and high collar in parchment and ink, in a diamond grid on plum-ink, with ravens, keyholes, quills and skull-moths between, the whole field breathing like candlelight. Drag to pan, double-tap to reseed the motifs. Drag to pan, double-tap to reseed.

title: Dandelion Medallions
note: After Julianne Haness's Dandelions: a purple vine scrollwork lattice on salmon framing giant coral dandelion medallions, crisp starbursts with dot fills, rotating slowly as the vines sway. Drag to pan, double-tap to reseed the medallions. Drag to pan, double-tap to reseed.

title: Snowy Owl Stare
note: After Julianne Haness's Snowy Owls: giant snowy-owl faces in half-drop repeat on gold-ochre, black brow wedges and orange eyes staring straight out, blinking one at a time on a slow stagger. Drag to pan, double-tap to change who blinks first. Drag to pan.

title: Prairie Plaid Bloom
note: After Suchita Prakash's prairie wildflower plaid: a hand-uneven woven plaid in wheat, denim and clay with flat wildflowers overflowing its lines, heads nodding in a slow wind wave. Tap to advance the plaid colours. Tap to re-colour the plaid.

title: Owl and Oak Damask
note: After Suchita Prakash's midnight owl and oak folk damask: a mirrored ogee lattice on navy whose motifs are heraldic owls with spread wings, oak sprays, acorns and crescent moons, breathing slowly while the owl eyes blink in sequence. Drag to pan the damask. Drag to pan.

title: Neon Midnight Garden
note: After Suchita Prakash's Neon midnight garden: dense flat neon florals, dahlias, sunflowers and moths in hot pink and violet on near-black, opening and closing in travelling waves. Drag through them and the blooms lean away and spring back. Drag to disturb the garden.

title: Harlequin Overflow
note: After Suchita Prakash's Merry Maximalist harlequin: a zero-margin diamond patchwork in hot pink, kelly and royal blue, every diamond holding one small Christmas vignette, some bleeding past their borders, the whole repeat slowly drifting. Drag to pan, double-tap to reshuffle the packing. Drag to pan, double-tap to reshuffle.

title: Colorway Machine
note: After Emi Bee's coordinate-family machine: one twisty floral sprig rendered twelve times in a grid, each cell a different curated colourway over its own ground, every cell breathing on its own phase. Drag sideways to scrub new colourways through the grid. Drag to re-colour.

title: Helmet Cats
note: After Emi Bee's MCM kitties: a parade of flat geometric cats marching across paper, circle heads and triangle ears, some in stroked-arc space helmets, tails swaying on a seamless loop. Watch only. Watch.

title: Murder in the Garden
note: After Emi Bee's Murder in the Garden: a poisonous-flower lattice on near-black, three of its thirty blooms blood red, with one tiny key and one small bird hidden among them and spores drifting over all of it on a twenty-four-second loop. Watch only. Watch.

title: Trinket Drape
note: After MyClayCo's trinket dishes: a twelve-petal dish seen from directly above on near-black, shaded in four flat teal bands, turning slowly while a ripple travels petal to petal on a twenty-eight-second loop. Watch only. Watch.

title: Red Triangle
note: After Arunima Dazess Wangchuk's degree show: a tall red-lit triangle in a black room, fire churning inside it, dark masks at its base with red-lit eyes, the edge light breathing on a thirty-second cycle. Watch only. Watch.

title: Raudra Roop
note: After Arunima Dazess Wangchuk's Raudra Roop: a wrathful glazed mask, crown of skulls and spiral brows, perfectly still while its turquoise glaze flows and pools in the crevices on a sixty-second loop. Watch only. Watch.

title: At Nature's Mercy
note: After Arunima Dazess Wangchuk's At Nature's Mercy: a sheer grey curtain in a dark room, one small black-and-white mountain low on the fabric, breathing almost imperceptibly on a forty-second cycle. Watch only. Watch.

title: Cartographies of Cloth
note: After Arunima Dazess Wangchuk's Cartographies of Cloth: felted contour lines in rust and terracotta with one dark river ribbon running the steepest path through them. Drag to raise the land and the river finds a new way down. Drag to reshape the terrain.

title: Fear Hope Field
note: After Arunima Dazess Wangchuk's two-pole palette: a stepped dye-lot field running diagonally from warning red to wellbeing teal, drifting on slow currents. Touch to resolve the colour where you press; double-tap for a new current. Touch the field; double-tap to reseed.

title: Swirling Vines
note: After Debbie Sharman's Swirling Vines: six jungle vines trailing down a cream ground, curling and unfurling at their tips, daisies and leaves at their nodes. Drag through them to bend them like wind. Drag to bend the vines.

title: Cockatoo Press
note: After Coral Cockatoo's brand bird: a sulphur-crested cockatoo in flat print colours on eucalyptus teal, crest rising and falling, perched on a diagonal branch. Tap for three quick head-bobs. Tap for a head-bob.

title: Crackle Screen
note: After Coral Cockatoo's Marble Crackle screen: a black crackle network printed flat on white, a window onto an endless field, a few cells tinted celadon. Drag to pan the field; tap for a new constellation. Drag to pan; tap to reseed.

title: Ditzy Field
note: After Coral Cockatoo's ditzy prints: a full field of teeny vermilion gum blossoms on cream paper, a slow swell wave crossing diagonally. Drag to press the motifs up to full size under your finger. Drag to press.

title: Potion Pair
note: After Xanthe Caesia's potion bottles: a raku black bottle and a cream cobalt-swirled bottle, linked by a gold thread between their corks, potion light glowing at each seam. Drag one and its pair follows; tap a cork for a pulse. Drag a bottle; tap a cork.

title: Marble & Transfer
note: After Xanthe Caesia's marbled mugs: brown-and-cream swirled clay with a crisp black silkscreen transfer, wattle, bee, banksia or butterfly, stamped over it. Drag to re-swirl the clay under the print; tap to stamp the next motif. Drag to stir the clay; tap to stamp.

title: Wagtail Loop
note: After Ali Fisher's willy wagtail: a black-and-white wagtail in white linework on deep navy, tail pumping in its real herky-jerky bursts, three, pause, two, over banksia pods and eucalyptus. Watch-only.

title: Honeyeater Perch
note: After Ali Fisher's native-bird flash: a New Holland Honeyeater in white linework on deep navy, bottlebrush at the branch tip, a small silvereye study below, one petal falling each loop. Watch-only.

title: Flash Drop
note: After Ruby Waters' flash sheets: nine creature motifs on cream, inked live one cell every four seconds: outline, flat colour flood, detail pass, holding as a finished sheet before washing back to bare outlines. Watch-only.

title: Okame Mask Field
note: After Ruby Waters' okame masks: eleven round moon faces with black bobs and high blush drifting at three depths over faint giant chrysanthemums, bobbing on staggered phases, one slow blink every eight seconds. Watch-only.

title: Wave Ground
note: After Ruby Waters' onna-musha painting: a warrior in vermilion and mint rides a still folk horse while the banded cobalt wave ground scrolls beneath, near rows faster than far. Watch-only.

title: Dala Engine
note: After Ruby Waters' Dala horse: a blocky painted toy horse, polka-dot fields and an S-curve flourish, its raffia tail a hundred swaying strands. Drag through the tail to part it; tap the saddle medallion to ripple its spots. Drag the tail, tap the medallion.

title: Kokeshi Stack
note: After Ruby Waters' kokeshi dolls: a moon-face doll on a cone body of stacked pattern bands, stripes, lotus, chrysanthemum and waves, a tiny Mt Fuji at its base breathing small clouds, swaying like a weeble. Watch-only.

title: Kawaii Vessels Grid
note: After Ruby Waters' Kawaii Vessels print: a 4x3 flash sheet of creature-vessels, planters, pots, a cat-lamp and an octopus-pot, blinking and swaying in slow cascade, each cell alive on its own phase. Watch-only.

title: Puffer Time
note: After Ruby Waters' puffer clock: a spiky tattoo-flash puffer, squiggle over dots, googly eyes tracking you, keeping real time from its brass centre. Drag a spike to wobble it; tap to puff. Drag to wobble, tap to puff.

title: Gold Seam
note: After Sophia Golovanevskaya's kintsugi repair philosophy: a dark vessel breaks along glowing seams and reassembles, each cycle leaving its gold lines behind. Tap to break it now; double-tap freezes the break. Tap to break, double-tap to hold the break.

title: Salt Worn
note: After Sophia Golovanevskaya's salt-eroded porcelain: a cream vessel whose lower half is pitted matte bone, its upper half holding a smooth teal glaze, a ragged shoreline between them where the tide breathes and slowly recedes, barnacles clinging along the line. Watch-only.

title: Basin Rings
note: After Njalikwa Chongwe's top-down basin: concentric glaze rings, an ochre rim, a celadon ring and a dark-red centre pool under a fine crackle, turning with glacial slowness, each ring at its own pace while the crackle holds still. Watch-only.

title: Terracotta Speckle
note: After Njalikwa Chongwe's terracotta range: a burnt-orange field of raw clay, dense with cream and dark speckle. Drag to stir the speckle into swirls; let go and it settles back to stillness. Drag to stir.

title: Target
note: After Njalikwa Chongwe's hand-painted medallions: a wobbly spiral target in terracotta, cream and cobalt on a crackled cream ground, green bleeding in at the rim, drawn stroke by stroke, ring by ring, the ochre spiral last. Watch-only.

title: Zigongo Bands
note: After Njalikwa Chongwe's banded vessels: a pot in side profile stacked with flat bands of coral, cobalt and emerald divided by black zigzag lines, one cream band in the stack. The bands rise slowly as if the vessel is being pulled from clay while its belly breathes. Watch-only.

title: The Clouds That Kept Us Grounded
note: After her Leh sky forms: heavy burnished stoneware clouds rest low over a dark Ladakhi ground, from days of staring at the sky and hoping the clouds don't clear. They drift almost imperceptibly while the low sun breathes across their surfaces. No interaction: stillness is the point. Watch-only.

title: Living Vessels
note: After Shupiwe Chongwe's Vessel at Likir: dozens of unfired clay vessels on stones in a dusty field under a low stone wall, each holding a hidden seed. Over about a minute the vessels weather, cracks spreading, surfaces darkening, and green shoots rise from the mouths. The piece never resets: time is the artist. Watch-only.

title: Winter Warrior
note: His 2022 bronze, monumental and still: a lone winter figure in heavy clothes and a big rounded fur hat, hands clasped, standing frontal on rough rock under a plain overcast sky. Almost nothing moves: a slow breathing rise and fall, and now and then a small wisp of breath fog. No pedestal, no turntable. Watch-only.

title: Chadar Balance
note: His chadar trek scrap porter: a small laden figure of rusted parts, glowing red headlamp, chain icicles dangling from the torso, jerrycan on its back, balanced high on tilted diamond plates of thin ice. The whole group sways a degree and a half on a twenty five second loop, chains swinging out of phase. A held breath. It never falls. Watch-only.

title: Path of Hope
note: The Path of Hope as the 1 by 4 metre chiffon banner reads: a winding trail of footprints in snow, heavy boots and light steps side by side, entering large in the foreground and curving up between dark rocky walls to distant blue peaks. The trail is a record, not an event: only a slow snowfall and a faint breathing of light move, over forty seconds. Watch-only.

title: Silhouette Signal
